about: The short text of each world for the text gallery (text/index.html, written by tools/build-deploy.mjs at every release): one to three sentences, 120 to 300 characters, plain words, present tense, what a visitor sees and the one idea that makes the world itself, as built. Where a world has no text here the page shows its caption (the `line` of its entry in src/worlds/index.js) if it has one.

texts.across-the-sea-of-ice: The storm never leaves the lake. Beyond it a valley climbs to a glacier of frozen waves and blue rifts, where one tall dark figure in a cloak goes bounding over the ice, and past that a ship lies locked in a frozen ocean with her lanterns lit.
texts.after-the-sixth-sun: Nobody here owns a lamp, because one of six suns has always been up. On this afternoon they set one by one and the red one left is eaten to a thread, while along the road the first torches ever lit are kindled. Then it goes out and the sky fills with stars.
texts.airbrush-black-hole: Flecks of paint keep streaking past the ship's chrome nose. They are overspray, and the whole sky is a 1970s paperback cover in spray paint, with toothbrush-spatter stars and a black hole that has the far side of its disc lifted over the top as an arch.
texts.alpenglow-horn: The eagle under us folds its wings and drops beside an avalanche. Far above, the last light of the evening is still on the top of a rock horn 1,500 metres tall.
texts.amber-reticulum: Morning sun catches the tops of limestone pinnacles. In the gullies between them lies one living thing, a net of glassy veins, and every few seconds its whole flow stops and runs back the other way.
texts.atlantic-falls-in: Open Atlantic swell with gannets flying alongside, until the water ahead tilts and runs downhill past the Rock into a Mediterranean that had dried to a salt desert.
texts.atoll-pass-shark-wall: The atoll has only one gap. The tide pours through it, and below the surface hundreds of grey reef sharks hang nose into the current in a sheet eighty metres wide, which opens to let us through and closes behind.
texts.attic-railway: From the footplate of a red tinplate express we follow a mouse through the tunnel in our headlamp and pass a town at window height. Then the track leaves the table on a trestle of matchsticks, and there are attic rafters where the sky was.
texts.aurora-fjord: A bull orca surfaces and blows on water so still that the northern lights lie in it whole, upside down. His fin cuts the reflection, a ring spreads from it, and the water goes flat again.
texts.azulejo-descent: Lisbon's old quarter is tiled in cobalt and white down to the paving, and the pictures move. A cat walks the housefronts and sails ride a storm, one tile at a time.
texts.back-to-us-above-the-fog: Nobody here shows a face. A man in a green coat stands on a crag above the fog, back turned, and under it six monks carry a coffin to a ruined abbey door.
texts.backlit-jade-range: The mountains are carved from jade. The light is behind the highest wall, so the stone glows wherever it is a few metres thick and stays nearly black where it is deep, and a line of bar-headed geese, us among them, climbs past it toward a pierced arch on the pass.
texts.ball-inside-the-small-flat: The house is tall and plain, the hallway dark. Behind the door a staircase far too long for the house runs down to a fireplace, and guests are climbing up out of it.
texts.bamboo-surf: The ground is ferns and a gully stream at first, with a typhoon bowing giant bamboo overhead. Then the stems ahead part like a curtain, we climb through, and the ground is the top of the forest, six metres below and rolling over ridge after ridge.
texts.banyan-homecoming: We are one flying fox among thousands. Home is a single banyan a kilometre across, entered by diving through the hole in its heart into a hall of pale root pillars with the colony hanging from the roof.
texts.bare-oilcloth-night: All the black is a tavern's oilcloth, left bare for the ground and every shadow. A white bear and wine jars as big as houses are brushed onto it in dry strokes.
texts.batik-monsoon: A wax line draws a scalloped outline on the sky and indigo dye floods in up to it, and so the monsoon front gains another cloud, made the way batik is made. Frigatebirds with red throat pouches fly ahead up a staircase of cloud toward the lip where it happens.
texts.beaded-sea: This ocean never pooled. It hangs over its own dry bed as hundreds of globes of water, each with the sky upside down in it. The largest is 500 metres across and has a coral reef glowing at its centre and outrigger boats sailing round its equator.
texts.bed-went-walking: Striding down the avenue is an empty brass bed, and its four jointed legs are still drawing out, collar by collar, from three storeys to 180 metres. The blocks ahead grow too, a storey at a time.
texts.blown-city: A steel blowpipe three metres thick comes down over the basin, and on its end is a bell tower 95 metres tall, still hot. The rest of the canal city is glass already.
texts.blue-cities-in-glass-globes: Each room of the iron museum has a great glass globe on a bronze stand, and the globes hold small blue cities, no two alike. One has a pond of jellyfish, another an avenue that elephants walk down. We end by diving into the largest through a bronze ring in its crown.
texts.blue-city-holi: Indigo and cobalt rooftops stretch a kilometre under a cliff-top fort, crossed at the height of a langur. The lanes send up plumes, powder on the day of Holi and bonfire smoke the night before.
texts.blue-riband-poster: Navy, teal, cream, gold and vermilion are the only inks, laid flat as on an art-deco travel poster, with a stipple where one tone steps to the next. They make a liner 310 metres long, her stern stepping down in five terraces, and the scallop waves marching past her.
texts.blue-sails-dry-sea: Where there was once a sea there is rippled sand with fossil ribs in it, and ships cross it on runners under tall sails of lit blue smoke. After sunset they come in to a white town whose harbour stairs end in sand, under two small fast moons.
texts.boat-with-no-one-aboard: At the bow of a worn pine barge a snapped tow rope swings. The barge is running out of a brown river mouth into seas that are each a single colour, one white and full of stars, one violet along a coast of giant flowers.
texts.boulders-that-walk: We are a burrowing owl, low over the Pampas in the last ice age. Our mate lands on a pale rock among the grass plumes and the rock stands up, back end first, a glyptodont that had been asleep under its shell.
texts.breakfast-table: China and gingham at sixty times their size, crossed at the height of a fly. Over a stack of pancakes, honey pours off a dipper in a seven-metre rope and coils where it lands.
texts.brick-outgrows-the-cloud: Thousands of builders no bigger than ants are at work on a spiral tower 520 metres high. Treadwheel cranes turn on its ledges, and at the summit the last stone of an arch is coming down on a rope.
texts.brimstone-parasol: There is no air on this moon. With no wind to bend it, a volcano's plume climbs 2,400 metres as a thin pencil and falls back as a ribbed umbrella five kilometres across, snowing in a ring where its rim lands.
texts.brinicle-ice-finger: Red starfish crawl away in time-lapse from a river of frost, and the slow ones turn white. It starts where a tube of ice, grown down from the Antarctic sea ice overhead, touches the sea bed.
texts.bubble-skin: The planet below is a soap bubble, the one sharp thing in a blurred garden. Its storms are swirls in the film, and it has seconds left before it bursts.
texts.cables-to-the-moon: The sun never sets on this forest, so the only way to night is up. We climb beside a seven-limbed plant hauling itself along a rope toward the Moon, and the sky goes dark while the leaves below stay in full day.
texts.canyon-of-light: Sun reaches the floor of this slot only where the walls draw apart, and there it comes down through the dust as a bright shaft with a pool of gold at its foot. We fly straight through one.
texts.canyon-of-three-airs: Boats float on gas. The canyon holds three kinds, too heavy to mix, lying one on another with surfaces that swell like water, and each hull sits in one with its keel hanging in the next. Further along, the same surface rolls up into a curl 150 metres tall.
texts.carded-moor: The hills are made of felt, and so are the hinds galloping beside the bog and the ewes by the burn. Beyond them a tor of stacked grey boulders has caught a cloud of fleece, which streams away on the wind.
texts.carillon-grove: We ride the bell-tender's balloon through a flooded forest of glass bells, where a single toll travels from bell to bell as a hopping gold light.
texts.carnival-on-the-frozen-river: On the river bed lies a boat that went down with its cargo of apples, and they are still red, spilled round a figure seated in the stern. All of it shows through ice as clear as dark glass, with skaters circling between lantern-hung booths on top.
texts.carousel-works: The carousel is only half built. It turns under test all the same, 86 metres across, and its animals come round in the order they are made, from glued boards through rough carving and primer to a last quarter hung with mirrors and lit bulbs.
texts.carved-house-in-snow: In the dovecote at the top of the house a thousand pigeons sit one to a niche. As the ramp comes up through its floor they lift ring by ring, the wave climbing the wall, and pour out through the one great window.
texts.cast-off-sound: On a northern coast knitted from chunky wool, the needles finishing the last headland are 300 metres long, and the ball of yarn feeding them is the size of a hill.
texts.castle-before-the-tide: We cross the beach at the height of a sand hopper, so a drip castle is a cathedral of eighteen spires. One is still being made, with wet sand dropping onto it from far overhead, and the tide is already running back into the three moats.
texts.cell-highway: A vermilion motor protein is walking a banded tube on two feet, leaving wet footprints and towing a bubble of cargo on a twisted tether. We ride on the bubble through a cell painted on rough paper, up to the one open pore in the nucleus.
texts.chains-turned-to-stone: Barges heaped with produce are moored among the columns of a hall, and swifts fly in through the roof. Under the black water the same hall hangs upside down as chains.
texts.chamak-road: A mountain highway above the Indus and a bridge full of oncoming trucks, with not a lamp on any of it. Their painted tin shows colour only where our two headlights reach.
texts.chambered-sun: Sailing boats cross a lake between terraces and white villages. The lake climbs the wall and fields close overhead, because the country lines a seashell the size of a moon, lit by a small sun inside.
texts.chandelier-city: Rain rises from the sea in tall shafts and koi swim in the cloud that serves as a ceiling. Under it the town hangs in gilded rings of lit windows.
texts.checkerboard-approach: Under the left wing of a landing jumbo we come in low over the roofs of Kowloon in the 1990s. At a hill painted in orange and white squares it banks hard right, then comes down between tower blocks higher than we are to a runway in the harbour.
texts.chinar-water-terraces: Halfway down a walled garden in Kashmir a kingfisher hangs on its wings over the canal, then dives. The canal ends as one sheet of falling water 16 metres high, with a gallery behind it and a black pavilion beyond.
texts.city-hung-below-its-net: Wind crosses the gap between two mountains in gusts and a whole town sways with it, canvas houses and hammocks hung on ropes from one great net with only cloud underneath.
texts.city-in-the-lake: Every four seconds a gold pendulum touches the lake from underneath. Its bell tower belongs to a city that is only a reflection, with nothing on the shore to cast it.
texts.city-on-stilts-above-the-cloud: Brass spyglasses are clamped to the rails of a town that stands above the cloud on a few thin legs. Each one is aimed down through a gap at the wood below.
texts.clipped-menagerie: No gardener is ever seen. A cut travels along the hedge, clippings shower down, and a shaggy lump beside the path turns out to have had a dove inside it.
texts.cloisonne-typhoon: Sea and storm cloud alike are cloisonné enamel, flat glassy cells with raised gold wire round each. Lightning is one more wire, branching inside the cloud.
texts.cloud-armada: In a two-deck wicker basket a crew in hats rides under the biggest of a hundred balloons. As we pass, its burner fires and it lights up like a paper lantern.
texts.cloudburst-local: Steam-age Bombay in the monsoon, from the open door of a suburban train. The line comes in on a brick viaduct over tin roofs and tarpaulins, then under three signal gantries into an iron shed full of steam.
texts.colossus-of-rhodes: We cross the harbour at the height of a ship's deck and go up one straight avenue through a town keeping a festival. At its head, where he may have stood, is a bronze sun god 32 metres tall, and the climb ends level with his chest.
texts.combed-sea: In Turkish paper marbling, pigment is dropped on water and raked into feathers. A whole northern sea is worked the same way. Boat hulls and shark fins do the raking, and where the tide runs between nine skerries the rocks serve as the teeth of a comb.
texts.comet-perihelion: Sunrise comes across the comet as a hard line of light, and the frost it touches smokes away within two seconds. Behind the line the vents go off one after another and a sixty-metre cliff slumps into its own fountain of ice. We leave on the blast, down the tails.
texts.corniche-120: One beat runs the whole of this neon coast. Gulls drawn as a single M flap once to it, and across the bay the skyline rises and falls as the bars of an equaliser.
texts.coronal-rain: Nothing on the Sun is solid. Its surface is a sea of glowing cells, each squeezed out by the next, and the arches standing on it are bundles of fine threads that rose-coloured rain slides down.
texts.country-in-squares: Skirt blown out behind her, a chess queen of red lacquer, 45 metres tall, runs flat out and never leaves her square. The grass streams past under her and a length of hedge keeps pace beside her.
texts.country-of-pins: Something the size of a hill is rolling under a plain of sliding metal pins, and all that ever shows of it is the dome of pins it lifts as it goes.
texts.country-with-no-up: A pentagon house hides nothing from overhead. Its rooms lie open, and so do the flat people walking past, each with a small light beating inside. Living in a plane, they have only ever seen one another edge on, as a single line of lights in fog.
texts.courts-in-the-attics: Past a court's attic offices and a dark cathedral with a candle as tall as a tree, a plain gate stands open in a high wall. Its keeper stands by it in a long fur coat, with an old man waiting on a stool at his side, and behind them is a second gate, larger, and then a third.
texts.crane-harbour: We go up by crane. It hoists us out of a canyon of stacked containers and runs us along its boom over a 400-metre ship, where six cranes work with their booms lowered like giraffes drinking and the idle ones raise theirs one after another.
texts.cranes-in-steam: One crane bows low, then springs straight up with its wings spread. Pairs are at it all along the gravel bar, in mist off a river that never freezes.
texts.crayon-house: Grass is a green strip along the bottom and sky is a strip along the top, the way a five-year-old draws them. The house leans, its front is only an outline, and a black cat as tall as the roof walks round it.
texts.crescent-over-yucatan: Over a shallow sea and its white sand hang two crescents. The smaller is the Moon. The other is a lumpy rock in the last forty seconds of its fall, and it keeps growing.
texts.curl-tree-winter: A bright line of fresh-cut wood climbs a bare pole, and behind it the pole springs open, tier by tier, into curls of shaving. A whole forest is being carved this way from one wood, with sawdust for snow.
texts.cut-from-the-sky: The doves are flat outlines filled with blue noon sky and white cloud, flying down a seaside street where it is night. Curtains at the head of the street are made of the same stuff, and the clouds inside them drift the opposite way to the clouds overhead.
texts.cut-mountain: An engraved tapir takes its colour, steps out of its ruled box and walks off along a ledge of the page. The page is the inside of a volcano sliced in half like a diagram, its caves and burrows shown in section.
texts.dawn-tracks-contrail: Other airliners creep across the sky, each at the head of its own line. We take one line the wrong way, from its frayed end to the four engines laying it.
texts.deer-cave-exodus: Thousands of bats make the river that runs under the roof of Deer Cave in Borneo. We leave as one of them, out through the mouth and straight at a full moon.
texts.delta-in-flood: Between the grass stems the whole plain is water, shallow enough to run through, and a herd hundreds strong is running. The spray they throw up hangs behind them in a wall several times their height.
texts.dew-garden: A ladybird more than a metre long climbs a blade of grass, then takes off and flies ahead of us past drops of water that each hold the lawn upside down.
texts.drafted-city: Even the trolley we ride is a drawing. It sketches itself around us while white lines rule a city onto blue paper and hatch in the shaded walls.
texts.dragon-kite-loft: On a trestle lies a disc of painted silk five metres across, tilted back like a roof tile. It is the tail of a dragon kite 120 discs long, threaded down a whole Weifang kite loft. When the line snaps taut the discs stand up in a wave, and we ride the last one out.
texts.dragons-blood-fog: Dragon's-blood trees stand on a plateau with fog running between their trunks. At the edge of a 300-metre cliff the fog pours over, and we go with it as a vulture.
texts.drawer-cliffs: The river runs between chests of drawers three hundred metres high. A drawer slides out with a pool and some grazing animals on it, the pool pours over the lip as a waterfall, and when the drawer slides shut the fall is cut off in mid-air.
texts.drowned-domes: Black ice lies over a flooded town, clear enough to show its streets. The onion domes of its churches stand up through the surface, and each is mirrored whole in it.
texts.drowned-forest-lakes: Dead trees stand bleached in a lake at Jiuzhaigou, dozens of them, and one huge fallen trunk makes an arch to pass under. The rest of the forest lies on the floor, which shows when a gust wipes the mirror off the water.
texts.ember-moon-tide: Fifteen times as wide as it looks today, the Moon hangs over an Earth with no ground and still glows red like a coal. The tide it pulls comes in as a swell fourteen metres high, breaking the thin crust on a sea of molten rock into plates with burning edges.
texts.emperor-clearing: Four thousand emperor penguins stand pressed into one dark crowd on the sea ice while a storm blows snow across their backs. When the wind drops, the snow draws off like a curtain and a wave of lifted beaks runs through them every four seconds.
texts.engine-turned-sea: Below lies a sea of hard enamel over engine-turned silver, its swell a pattern of cut lines that catch the light. Eggs up to 90 metres tall stand in it on their own reflections, and the greatest, 170 metres, opens like a flower to show a small gold clockwork bird.
texts.engraved-sea-chart: Drawn in the ink lines of a copperplate chart, the swells roll as moving hatching. A sea serpent stands out of the water in three arches 45 metres high, and the ship sails under the middle one.
texts.evening-is-the-beam-tipping: We are a speck of dust adrift inside a hanging mobile. A moth flies in and settles on one of the painted wooden clouds, and the cloud sinks under its weight.
texts.every-wingbeat-stays: Nothing that moves over these dunes can leave its past behind. Runners trail a colonnade of their own legs, and a climbing bird a whole arcade of wings.
texts.false-stars: Glow-worms light the roof of a New Zealand cave and still water doubles them, so a black kayak with no lamp floats in the middle of a ball of blue points.
texts.fern-sea-midnight: Ducks on stilt legs sit in rafts on what could pass for a meadow, until the swell comes through and lifts them. Under the fern lies the polar ocean of 49 million years ago, free of ice, and a herd of hornless brontotheres is wading across the bay.
texts.field-in-thick-paint: Morning sun comes in low over a hay meadow made of oil paint, each blade of grass a single brush stroke as long as a street, wet enough still to shine.
texts.field-of-doors: Doors without walls, about ten thousand of them, stand in the grass at dusk, each laying the light of another sky on the ground. The last is 400 metres tall and ajar.
texts.figure-and-ground: A shoal rises through the sea in files, and at the surface each fish rolls a quarter turn and locks into place like a tile. The gaps between them are the shapes of geese seen from above, and in straight lines those gaps thicken into birds and fly off.
texts.fire-in-the-sand-sea: A line of three-toed prints walks down the rose sand and into lava. The prints are old. Sheet lava is filling every hollow of the desert, leaving each dune ridge an island with a thin line of fire round it, and the dinosaurs that leave such prints are running uphill.
texts.fireworks-under-the-wash: Drawn in candle wax on white paper, the garden hardly shows. Then dark ink floods through from behind, runs off the wax, and a palace of fire stands out in seven arches.
texts.first-rain-palace: Nine cloud elephants, 33 times life size, walk trunk to tail along the skyline behind the hills of Udaipur, and the rain sky rolls out from under their feet. On the lake below, a royal barge rows past a white marble island palace, and the lightning is gold leaf.
texts.first-rain-stepwell: This well in Rajasthan is 65 metres deep, its walls cut into ten thousand steps. Rain breaks while we are inside, and each step becomes a waterfall.
texts.first-snow-on-kraft: Falling snow is the white pencil. Each stroke comes down, stops along a bough or a wall top and stays there, and the tree whitens limb by limb as we pass.
texts.five-colour-river: Out of a round well in the riverbed two giant otters stand up to watch us skim past. The rest of the family is racing down the channel, through the red weed of Caño Cristales in Colombia.
texts.fleet-in-six-wools: Paired beasts pace on the spot in the two borders, and each horse on the shore has its far legs in a different wool from its near ones. The fleet beyond stands on plain cloth, since no wool is used to fill sea or sky.
texts.flinching-forest: Each cloud drags a clearing across the land. The trees are plume-worms in tall tubes, and where the shadow falls they screw down out of sight, leaving bare pipes that fill again slowly once the sun is back.
texts.flying-boat-karst-bay: The rock is limestone, in sheer towers with jungle on top, and a 1930s seaplane spirals down between them to land. We ride outside, on its float strut.
texts.fog-river-bridge: Fog lies in the strait so deep that a ship goes under the bridge with only the top of her showing. Six pelicans glide in a line ahead of us, and we are the seventh.
texts.fogged-palm-house: Drops run down the misted panes of a winter glasshouse, each ruling a clear stripe that fogs over again behind it. A leaf is sharp and green only where it touches the glass or comes within arm's reach.
texts.folding-market: Cloth awnings roof a Thai market lane with a railway down the middle. They swing up in a wave just ahead of the railcar's buffers and drop shut again behind it.
texts.forest-from-a-drop: It rains in heavy dark drops over a country of glazed, slip-banded pots as big as hills, and wherever one lands on a wet band, a tree branches out of the blot.
texts.forest-tied-from-above: Two bundles of a thousand ropes each are tying a single square knot, and we pass through its eye as it draws tight. Nothing stands. Trunks of knotted rope hang from out of sight and trail their tassels in a flat sea.
texts.forty-four-sunsets: No bigger than a house, the planet does not turn, so one side of it is always day and the other always night. A wooden chair stands on the line between, facing the sun, and a rose grows under a glass globe just inside the dark.
texts.four-colour-launch: Printed in ink dots on newsprint like a pulp magazine, twelve ships lift off one after another while a rocket sled runs the rail between their pads.
texts.four-stone-kings-over-the-river: White water breaks round boulders of black granite, then the river runs smooth past honey sand and a small white steamer tied to the bank. Ahead the cliff is cut into seated figures 24 metres tall, one broken at the chest.
texts.frieze-without-end: A seal stone tall as a cathedral rolls over a plain of wet river clay, and each turn prints the same raised picture, a mountain between two beasts and a rayed sun disc. Behind it the prints dry from dark to pale, and then the seal slows and comes to rest.
texts.frozen-weather-museum: Sparrows fly about the halls among weather that does not move. A shower hangs in mid-fall and a tornado stands in the rotunda with a small wooden house in the air beside it, each starting up only as we reach it. The end wall is a hurricane, mounted like a painting.
texts.gale-in-green-glass: A three-masted ship is riding out a storm inside a bottle that lies on a study table. Beyond its wall the room stands huge, a lit lamp on one side and shelves of books on the other, and a pale moth walks on the outside.
texts.galimoto-yard: Along one side of a swept yard runs a whitewashed wall, and on it the shadows of some forty bent-wire toys join into one line drawing of a street.
texts.galleon-in-the-flowers: Small yellow flowers fall through a wet forest and over a Spanish ship that stands whole and chalk white in a clearing, many days from any sea.
texts.gannet-stack-gale: Gannets fish by falling. Off the sea stack where they nest, thirty of them tip over in a gale and go down together through the surface, trailing bubbles.
texts.garden-carpet: The cat on the rug is asleep. Down at the height of an ant, the rug's woven garden stands up out of the pile as we cross it, with cypresses of knotted wool and a fountain of silk thread, then sinks back flat.
texts.garden-in-plan: The pool is carved as seen from above, its ducks and fish from the side. Trees lie flat round it, crowns outward, and swing upright in rows as the skiff passes.
texts.garden-of-sixty-gardens: Over a plain of ponds hangs a hollow globe 300 metres across, faceted like a paper lantern, its inside lined with more ponds and leaning trees. There is only one small garden here. Three mirrors make the rest.
texts.garden-upside-down: One elm hangs by its roots, crown down, like a chandelier over open sky. The meadow it grows from is the ceiling, the clouds are the floor and the sun is below them.
texts.gates-in-the-snow: Two runs of glowing scrollwork race along the railings of a public garden forged from black iron bar, winding each curl shut and shedding the snow from every rail they heat. They climb a pair of gates ninety metres tall, finish the crown and swing the leaves open.
texts.geode-run: The cavern is a hollow egg of crystal 175 metres tall. A timber trestle winds down the inside of it on stilts and chains, and the ore cart on the rails is a runaway.
texts.gilded-margin: The page is still being made. To a bee crossing it, the vines along its edge are putting out leaves and a goose quill 200 metres long sweeps overhead laying a wet black line. Low on the page stands a letter O in gold leaf, dull brown until the light strikes it.
texts.glass-nave: Doves go up in a spiral from between the pews, and we climb after them to the height of a rose window eighteen metres across. The sun is behind its twelve petals, and its blues and rubies hang in the incense.
texts.glass-painted-fleet: The fishing beach of Saint-Louis, Senegal, painted on the back of a sheet of glass. More than two hundred pirogues lie side by side with their bows to the surf.
texts.glaze-stops-at-the-knees: Glaze is still running down the horse. It is a pottery horse 190 metres tall, standing on its slab with a loaded camel and ranks of ponies, and on all of them the amber and green give out at a ragged line on the legs, leaving bare pink clay below.
texts.glider-country: Glazed cubes like ceramic toy blocks stand on a tiled plain, and each one is a cell in a running game of Life. Where two crescents of low cubes close on each other, a five-cube walker drops out and sets off down a street of old towers with cube trees on their roofs.
texts.glowwood: Six-legged animals drink at a stream that glows teal, under giant mushrooms with lit gills. Beyond them the forest opens round one tree whose canopy is thousands of hanging pink threads, a weeping willow in fibre optics, with gold light running down it in pulses.
texts.great-refractor: A pale moth a metre and a half across climbs the bar of starlight towards the slit in an observatory dome, and six more come up behind it. The observatory is an 1890s one at twelve times life size, which makes the white telescope beside them 204 metres long.
texts.green-with-the-rain: One thin sheet of copper, hammered from behind into a northern city of gables and spires. Rain crosses it in a line and leaves the roofs verdigris.
texts.groundswell-country: A herd has to gallop just to stay on one crest, because the hills here travel like ocean swells. Woods ride them and the meadow breaks as surf.
texts.hail-cathedral: Lightning starts low in the wall of a storm's updraft and runs up the spiral, lighting the cloud from inside, buttress by buttress. We are a hailstone rising past it.
texts.hall-of-strings: We are inside a grand piano while someone plays it. At this size the bass strings are cables hundreds of metres long, and any string that has just been struck blurs into a ribbon of light and then fades.
texts.halls-between-sea-and-cloud: Six halls of stone lie in a straight line, their walls set tier above tier with white marble statues. In one the sea stands still, waist-deep round the lowest figures. In another it comes in through eight tall doors, wave after wave, and runs back out.
texts.hammam-of-stars: Steam is filling the hot room of a Damascus bathhouse before it opens. As it thickens, sunlight from glass eyes in the dome, cut as stars and hexagons, shows up beam by beam and grows down to the wet marble. The way in is by copper bathing bowl along the water channel.
texts.hanging-gardens-of-babylon: Five planted terraces above a brown river, as the gardens may have stood on a spring evening. The flight glides down to a black quay, climbs a long stair past each dripping level and walks under cedars to an arched door in the palace wall.
texts.hanging-sea-lilies: The flowers are animals. Sea lilies trail from a drifting conifer trunk on jointed ropes up to 18 metres long, crowns downward, over water with no floor in sight.
texts.harbour-of-one-lamp: Afterglow, and a stone fishing town with its shutters closed. One window high under the hill is lit, and its gold lies in one long streak down the bay.
texts.heavy-things-on-a-sheet: Each ball sits in its own dent. The cloth is the one a teacher stretches to show gravity, ruled in lines 40 metres apart and as wide as a sky. We follow a glass marble round the deepest dent, a bowling ball's, while a golf ball rolls in and sinks it further.
texts.honey-cliff: A honey buzzard wheels off the combs it has been raking, twelve gold half-moons hung under an overhang and cloaked in black bees. We are one of the bees, flying home.
texts.hoopwind-flats: Shadows on this salt pan are coloured, because the animals that throw them are rolling rims of horn with tinted skin inside. Where shadows cross, the tints mix.
texts.house-behind-the-waterfall: A troop of monkeys has the run of a mountain stream and of the stone hall inside the cliff at its head. Their way in is a leap through the waterfall.
texts.house-in-the-niche: On a sill in a wall of plaster niches, a model house stands with its door open. It is a model of the Lamu merchant's house whose upper room it sits in, and through its door is that same room, later in the day, with its own model. Five rooms in, it is night.
texts.house-of-four-seasons: Snow lies under the moon in one court while, in the garden beside it, maples stand red in a low sun. The same estate has a spring lake with painted boats and a summer dusk of fireflies, and each garden keeps its own season with the other three alongside.
texts.house-opens-seaward: On a white beach a long Malay timber house stands shut on its stilts, hens in the sand out front. The breeze arrives when we do and throws its shutters wide, bay after bay.
texts.hull-in-frames: We ride a steaming plank of ironwood down the middle of a ship that stands in frames in a Sulawesi boatyard. Seventy pairs of them curve up on either side, and at the bow the plank is bent to their curve and pegged, three knocks to a peg.
texts.hull-town: The shipbreakers' shore kept its ships. They sit on the mud as a town, with washing strung from hull to hull and lifeboats left hanging at the rail as balconies, and the funnels smoke because someone below is cooking.
texts.hundred-layer-red: Colour is how deep the knife went. The land is one solid block of lacquer with no air in it, cut down to green for water and buff for sky, and it goes on cutting itself ahead of us and healing over behind, round a peony 180 metres across in nine tiers of petals.
texts.ice-arcade: Birch by birch the ice lets go. A sheath bursts from foot to tip, the shards come down in a curtain, and the freed trunk whips back up and stands rocking.
texts.indigo-pits: A cloth forty metres long is hauled out of the dye without pause, yellow-green at the surface, emerald at six metres and full indigo before it reaches the drum.
texts.ink-dragon: A far peak begins as a faint stain. It floods dark and dries sharp as we come near, and above the mist a dragon 320 metres long, drawn in a single brushstroke, coils round a pavilion on a summit and then paints a circle in the air with its tail.
texts.inside-out-world: The river never ends. It follows the floor of a spinning ring two kilometres in radius, up one horizon, across the sky as a silver thread and down the other.
texts.iron-tide: Under a sky tiled in metal leaf lies a mirror sea of black magnetic fluid. Wherever a floating lodestone passes over, the fluid stands up in spikes and follows it.
texts.island-being-born: At wave height, along a raft of floating pumice, towards an island three weeks old and still blasting itself out of the sea. A surge cloud rolls over us in the breach, and the climb out runs between a trunk of black ash and one of white steam.
texts.island-that-shades-the-fields: Farms and a village on a plain stretch of coast, with boats offshore. Over them hangs a round island of rock 440 metres across, its underside a mirror with the sea in it.
texts.islands-in-custard: Meringue for the islands, which bob like corks, and custard for the sea. The rest is caramel, which comes down from the sky in thin threads and is flung over the biggest of them in hundreds of arcs that set as a cage.
texts.isle-of-broken-towers: Fifty metres of ruined tower stands on an island far out to sea, and the grey shape wound round it is a dragon 170 metres long. It rears above the top and breathes fire.
texts.jungle-he-never-saw: Monkeys sit in a tree and a tawny cat looks out of the leaves, much as in any jungle. The lotus flowers are the odd part, each as big as a house on a jointed stalk taller than the trees, with one more monkey sitting in the heart of the highest.
texts.kelp-cathedral: Through shafts of sun and rows of giant kelp that reach from the sea bed to the surface, a humpback and her calf swim down the aisle. She breaches, seen from underneath.
texts.khlong-run: Seven silk ribbons stream back from the garlanded prow of a long-tail boat as it races down a canal in old Bangkok, under washing lines and eight low footbridges, and out onto the open river toward a temple spire.
texts.knotted-river: The river has no banks. It hangs in the sky, a rope of water in a trefoil two kilometres across, and boats sail right round it because down is toward its middle.
texts.kohbar-lotus-room: On one end wall a painted elephant lifts its trunk. On the other a wheel of six lotus leaves turns about a bamboo stem, and fish swim along the walls between, in a mud house in Mithila made ready for a wedding.
texts.kolam-at-dawn: A sparrow as big as a house drinks from the rim of a brass pot. We are ant-sized on a wet Tamil doorstep, where a thread of rice flour falls from overhead and runs its pattern through a grid of dots.
texts.kurbits-night: Eight tiers of invented flowers go up a single stem from a two-handled urn on a village green. All of it is Swedish folk painting, each petal a separate brush stroke laid on while we climb past on a painted bird.
texts.ladder-orchard: Hair-thin ink ladders grow in rows out of a ragged island of red earth. There is no horizon, only a wash of stain on all sides and underneath. The longest ladder is 480 metres, with a red sun and a black crescent balanced off it like a mobile.
texts.lake-comes-down-in-curls: For eighty metres the water falls in plaited locks, each strand drawn like combed hair. A high lake has broken through its wall of rock, and the pool underneath winds the current outward in long spirals round a boil.
texts.lake-dyed-three-times: Dye soaks up through a valley made of hanging silk threads, rising from the waterline into the slopes. The waterline is only a fold, where each thread turns back and hangs again as its own reflection, so the mirror is dyed with the rest.
texts.lake-of-pink-fountains: A goldfinch 20 metres tall tugs a seed from a thistle head, then drops off and dives down the tilted lawns to the lake, over orchard trees half its height.
texts.lamps-among-golden-leaves: Lamps of three colours, gold, silver and leaf green, hang from the platforms of a town built in the crowns of silver-barked trees. Rope ladders come down to the ground and no walkway joins one tree to the next.
texts.lantern-river: Paper lanterns are lifting off the boats and quays of an old river town by the thousand, amber against the blue of early night. At the bend a nine-tier pagoda hung with some 400 red ones stands over its own image, upside down in the water.
texts.lanterns-under-ice: The sea bed is pillow lava and smoking mineral chimneys, under a black ocean sealed inside a moon's frozen shell. Hundreds of amber jellyfish rise through it, and an eel-whale 140 metres long swims over us with its orange heart beating through its skin.
texts.last-lit-windows: The sun has gone out. One pyramid, miles high, holds everyone who is left, and they stand at its windows, floor after floor, looking out at the dark.
texts.leaded-forest: Light comes only from behind, as through a window. Each leaf is a pane of coloured glass in black lead, and four seasons pass across the forest.
texts.lemon-cliffs: From a step in an alley a cat watches a paper plane go. It comes out 150 metres above the sea and circles down a cliff of pastel houses to the fishing boats.
texts.lens-works: A moth circles the oil lamp inside a great glass optic, built for a lighthouse and under test in a Paris workshop of the 1860s. The hall is 25 times life size, so we are no bigger than the moth.
texts.light-from-the-left: Cloud is passing over the house, and the light under each leaded window swells and fades in turn along a white room. Out through the open casement, the same cloud leaves one strip of sun running along the harbour roofs.
texts.light-in-every-dark-place: Fire-lit windows line the snowing street, the frozen moor beyond it has one lit hut, and out at sea the fire is down to a slit in a tower and a ship's lanterns.
texts.line-along-the-river-of-stars: Water, clear and glowing over a bed of burning sand, is what the Milky Way is made of here. A small old train with yellow windows follows its bank through silver grass and gentians.
texts.line-through-the-hill: A hill is a black tunnel mouth with pencil arcs drawn round it, one outside the next, on scrap paper pasted together. There is no sky, only more paper.
texts.litho-medusae: Sixty metres wide to anyone the size of plankton, the great jellyfish is a natural-history print of about 1900 come alive in flat inks. The way to it runs through a glass shell as big as a house and up into its mouth.
texts.long-library: Afternoon sun falls through high windows in shafts thick with dust. Under them a hall of bookshelves runs a quarter of a kilometre to a rotunda, where brass arms carry six enamelled planets round a sun of amber glass.
texts.longest-animal: Sixty-four glass bells pump at the head, and behind them the same animal runs on for more than a hundred metres, coiled in black water like a galaxy. A curtain of fine threads hangs under it, baited with ember lures.
texts.macaw-wall: We follow two macaws down a brown Amazon river to the cliff where the rest are, hundreds hung in pairs on red clay. An eagle's shadow slides along the wall and it empties over our heads, a sheet of birds against the sky.
texts.maelstrom-descent: Six hundred metres from rim to rim, the whirlpool has a wall of clear water with fish hanging inside it. A sailing boat slides round it, down to the throat.
texts.malecon-norther: We drive a 1950s convertible flat out along a Caribbean seafront with the top down. Swells hit the seawall and go up in white fans that lean over the road, and one of them comes down on the car.
texts.mammoth-midnight-sun: Saiga antelope at a flat run meet woolly mammoths at a walk. The herd squeezes through the gaps in the line, under tusks and past knees, and closes up beyond.
texts.manta-cyclone: About two hundred manta rays turn in a single hollow column, and we rise up the inside of it against the turn, so that each animal arrives mouth first.
texts.maple-gale: One sugar maple, 28 metres tall, leans out over the lip of a waterfall and loses its leaves in two seconds. We are the gust that takes them.
texts.mara-crossing: The waterfall on this bend of the Mara River is made of wildebeest, going over a twelve-metre bank of red earth without stopping. We run with them and jump in just upstream.
texts.marigold-way-home: Pots simmer on the kitchen stove and a dog lies in the patio. From the street door a road of glowing orange petals runs through the house to an altar of seven tiers and some six hundred candles.
texts.mausoleum-at-halicarnassus: The chariot on top of the tomb is empty, because nobody knows who rode in it. Four marble horses stand before it, on a stepped roof over a ring of 36 columns.
texts.mayfly-bloom: Cut glass, layer on layer, lit from behind like a vase with a lamp in it. The river inside hatches all its mayflies in one evening, and we go upstream as one of them.
texts.mended-country: Fired clay and glaze make the ground, the inside of one broken bowl two kilometres wide. Molten metal runs uphill along the cracks and draws the shards together.
texts.milky-sea: On the Arabian Sea, with no moon, the water is brighter than the sky. A becalmed barque stands on the glow, slack sails lit from underneath on masts up to 44 metres tall.
texts.million-mirrors: Two pierced cedar doors swing open on a Persian room faced in mirror, cut small and set at angles across five honeycomb domes, so the glitter never holds still.
texts.mirror-chimneys: Hot water floats on cold. Two kilometres down, in lamp light alone, it gathers under each stone shelf of a 55-metre vent chimney and lies against the rock dead level, shining like mercury, with the red-plumed tubeworms beneath it reflected the wrong way up.
texts.mola-reef: A dugout canoe floats overhead on a ceiling of cloth, its paddle dipping. Under it the Caribbean sea bed is stitched in the layered, cut-through needlework of the Guna people, down to the hawksbill turtle.
texts.monarch-sanctuary: Monarchs roost on the firs so thickly that each limb hangs like wet thatch, brown with shut wings. In the air above the stream they are a river of orange, and a limb they have left stands a good deal straighter.
texts.moon-in-dry-dock: Laundry is strung across the street and a cat sleeps on a barrel. Down at the harbour the Moon is up on keel blocks, getting a new coat of silver leaf.
texts.moon-in-every-paddy: One frog jumps off a dyke and the moon in that paddy breaks into sliding bars. Hundreds more flooded terraces step down the mountain, each holding a moon of its own.
texts.moon-jar-kiln: Twelve chambers long, the kiln is half a kilometre of hillside to a sparrow, which is our size. Fire climbs it room by room, turning chalk-white jars gold.
texts.moor-under-the-fog-bank: Fog lies low and level in a hollow of the mire, a bank that stays where it is. Along its foot a huge black dog gallops to and fro, pale blue fire streaming from its mouth and lighting the pools and the edge of the fog.
texts.morning-after-the-gale: A court lady sits behind a reed blind with her back turned, eleven robe hems showing one inside another under a fall of black hair. She is thick old paint on paper. When a gust rolls the blind up, flakes of her colours come away and blow off.
texts.moss-rain-veranda: Paper screens slide away ahead of us and a Kyoto temple hall lies open, its black lacquer floor holding a second, upside-down copy of the wet garden outside.
texts.mother-of-pearl-shoal: Seabirds plunge into a black lacquer sea and we follow them down to a turning ball of sardines, each a chip of cut shell. Gold sailfish slash at it, then a gold whale comes up underneath and takes half in one lunge.
texts.mud-tower-haboob: Some forty kites stand on their strings over a town of mud-brick towers. The dust coming up the canyon is 800 metres high, and its wind takes the kites first.
texts.natron-liftoff: Flamingos need a run-up. Thousands patter across the red brine of Lake Natron ahead of a low biplane, each footfall a white splash, and lift in a wave.
texts.neon-monsoon: A koi 120 metres long swims up a street of towers at night. It is only projected light, so the rain falls straight through it and so do we, out by the tail.
texts.net-on-the-vault: Light off water, drawn as netting. Cords of it meet three to a knot and slide across the brick vaults and along the hulls of ninety-six moored skiffs.
texts.net-up-the-pillar: Four men walking a capstan wind us 246 metres up the face of a rock pillar, in a slow circling on the rope, and in through a hatch in the floor of their hoist house.
texts.night-by-the-slice: A knife is being laid down on a board beside a loaf of clear dark jelly a kilometre long, with a night sky set inside it. Five slabs stand already cut, a fuller moon in each, and the newest is still wobbling.
texts.night-under-the-oaks: Sunlight covers the meadow, hard and high, and stops at the trees. Each has a dome of night with stars in it for a shadow, and under the oak deer lie asleep.
texts.nobody-up-yet: On the bluff stands a clapboard hotel 170 metres long and a single room deep, so behind its windows there are more windows, each holding a square of sea.
texts.obsidian-forge: The moon is in pieces and most of the light comes up from the ground. A river of lava comes down from a fountain 300 metres high, between walls of six-sided basalt columns and past blades of black glass that stand on its banks like sails.
texts.octilinear-city: The city has no buildings and is made of its own transit map, lifted off the page in nine colours. A round black point is still ruling the end of one line.
texts.oculus-day: The hours go by in seconds under a Roman dome six times life size, and the one beam from the hole in its crown crosses the walls like a clock hand.
texts.old-light-arriving: One amber globe, small enough to hold in a lap, glows without a flicker. Thousands like it line the stone tiers of a bowl hollowed out of a hill in the river, and the crowd holding them sits still, watching a new star that stands low in the sky.
texts.one-bit-moonrise: The sea is rows of dashes, and under an enormous moon they join into a solid road. Sailing boats cross it, each drawn in the opposite ink to whatever lies behind, so a hull halfway onto the road is two-toned.
texts.one-standing-place: Paintings are stretched across the walls and vaults of an empty convent, and each comes right from one spot only. There the long smears slide together into a sphere of rings or a laurel wreath, then pull apart.
texts.orbit-dawn: The sun comes up behind the turning wheel of a space station, and its spokes blot it out one by one in passing. We go through between two of them, past a rim with gardens and trees lit behind its windows.
texts.out-the-nursery-window: The hours are places. Night stays over the town and day is a white cloud bank out at sea, with great white birds asleep in it on spread wings. Past the cloud lies one small island where a low sun never goes down, gold on one side and violet shade on the other.
texts.over-the-rim: A cable car crosses a market of striped tarpaulins on flat ground, then the ground ends and a brick city fills the canyon below, 400 metres deep.
texts.painted-ridges: Two ears and a stiff dark mane stay at the bottom of the view. We are riding a takhi, a wild horse, inside its galloping herd on a crest of striped rock.
texts.painted-shadow-town: Nothing casts a shadow among these leaning canvas house fronts. Light and dark are brushed on in chalk and black, and stay put while the cloth bellies in a draught.
texts.painted-where-you-stood: Paint spread across the floor and up one wall of a white hall adds up to a valley, but only from a single spot. A few metres on, its river lies flat on the flagstones.
texts.paper-boat-rapids: Twelve centimetres of folded cream paper rides a flooded gutter. From just behind the stern, the kerb is a cliff and the storm drain a waterfall under a gas lamp.
texts.paper-kingdom: Three hundred metres wide, a pop-up book lies open in a valley of creased white hills. Its city springs up off the pages in a wave, and about a thousand folded cranes pour out through a round hole cut in a standing page.
texts.pastel-bulb-fields: Nothing dark is ever drawn on these pastel bulb fields, so a shadow is the paper showing through. Under the first windmill the shadows of its four sails sweep the bank, and each flower is rubbed out as a bar crosses it, then stroked back in.
texts.patio-of-pots: One wall holds about a thousand clay pots on iron rings, thirty rows of them, most planted with geraniums. The shadow of the roof opposite lies across it, and because hours pass in seconds its edge moves down the rows fast enough to watch.
texts.pedalling-bones: Skeletons in bowlers and sombreros cycle down a tram avenue. Their bones are the cheap dyed paper itself, left bare inside a black outline, like the sky.
texts.pelican-collage: The pelicans fish in a horseshoe. They are jointed toys of torn, hand-painted tissue, like the reeds and water of the Danube delta around them, and the dip of their bills runs round the arc from one tip to the other as a wave of raised wings.
texts.pencil-test-rays: Pencil on a flat sheet of paper, twelve drawings a second, the way an animator tests a scene. Each leap is planned as an arc and a row of ovals, then a shaded ray jumps it and rubs the plan out.
texts.petal-storm: The stream carries rafts of fallen cherry petals, and more lie in drifts under the groves of Mount Yoshino. One gust lifts them all, and the ground turns from pink to green while the trees keep their blossom.
texts.pharos-of-alexandria: Gulls wheel round the lowest stage of the tower and merchant ships ride at anchor off the tip of the quay with their sails furled. It is the end of a midsummer day. At the top, about 110 metres up, a bronze figure with a staff stands over a ring of steady fire.
texts.pier-comet: Sixty metres across, the wheel beside the pier has no hub and no spokes, only a white ring hung with gondolas. A wooden roller coaster, its last rails held up by one thin mast, dives through the empty middle.
texts.pillar-of-the-white-night: A fjord in Norway on a midsummer night, the horizon held fifteen degrees above level so that the sea stands up like a wall. On it the moon's reflection is a gold column of one width, round at the top.
texts.pillars-before-trees: Four hundred million years ago no plant grows above the waist, and the tallest living thing on Earth is a bone-pale column 8.8 metres high, smoking spores.
texts.plain-of-fans: A kilometre wide and always moving, the pattern on the ground is made of animals. Thousands of suitors open and turn their fans together for the flock overhead.
texts.plain-with-two-sides: A white road crosses La Mancha with a different country on each side. Where an inn stands on the left, a castle with silver pinnacles stands on the right, and where sheep graze, an army waits under banners.
texts.pneumatic-emporium: We go the way the money goes in a Buenos Aires department store of 1910, as a brass capsule fired up a glass tube from the basement to the cashier's cabin.
texts.pointillist-nursery: Stars, dust and the gas between them are all dabs of paint, twelve pigments and never a mixed one. Near the dust pillar they come apart and pass on either side of us.
texts.pond-drop: A dive into a lily pond keeps going, and we shrink as it does. A tadpole passes like an airship, and further down a hollow green ball of some two thousand algae cells rolls on its axis while we fly in at one pole and out at the other.
texts.pond-with-no-water: Lotus leaves stand on stalks far too long and a fish hangs in bare paper, eye rolled up at us. It is a pond brushed in ink with the water left out.
texts.prismatic-dawn: A hot spring 110 metres across lies in rings of colour, and the steam lifting off each ring takes that ring's colour. Bison stand in the steam along its edge.
texts.rainbow-bridge-scroll: We ride a grain barge down a river ruled in ink on a strip of silk. At the timber bridge the mast comes down a metre short of the beams while a crowd leans over the rail.
texts.raising-the-ger: A ger is putting itself up on the Mongolian steppe, ten times life size. Eighty-one roof poles swing over into the crown wheel, and felt closes the sky down to one beam of sun.
texts.red-drive-down-to-the-sea: Beeches roof a winding drive like a nave, then give way to rhododendron, two towering walls of one deep red with a long grey house small in the gap at the end.
texts.red-sails-dawn: North Texas, 280 million years ago, long before any dinosaur. Sail-backed animals stand side-on to the dawn in knee-deep mist, and a level line of sunlight comes down through all their sails together.
texts.redwood-dawn: Pale mushrooms glow on a floor of moss and ferns, between walls of cracked charcoal. The floor is the inside of a fallen tree 120 metres long, burnt hollow, in a grove where the standing trunks are wider than houses.
texts.reindeer-cyclone: Each of some three thousand reindeer keeps to its own ring on a frozen lake. The outer ones trot, the inner ones walk, and at the centre calves lie in the snow round a boulder split in two by frost.
texts.reverse-angle: Two white feather tips keep flicking into the top of the view as an October valley goes by underneath. Then the picture cuts to the far end, where a child at a hayloft door, red mittens on the sill, is watching a white speck in the sky. The speck is us, a homing pigeon.
texts.ring-run: At the edge of a giant planet's rings the ice rubble stands up in waves that curl over like breakers, each stone streaming up the face and over the crest. A skiff gets there flat out, across the ring and then down through it.
texts.ringed-shore: Twenty-five metres tall on four stilt legs, an animal wades a tidal flat so wet it mirrors the whole dusk sky. Each footfall sends ripples out through the reflection of a giant planet and its rings.
texts.river-that-sinks-under-the-garden: Rocks come up with the water. A fountain bursting from a cleft in a cedar hill throws them about, and the river it starts winds through walled gardens to a gold and lapis dome, then drops into the cliff of ice beneath.
texts.roll-top-harbour: Beyond a town cut from veneer the sea is wooden slats, like the shutter of a roll-top desk. It runs flat from the quay, then turns upward between two runners and curls back overhead to a lip 440 metres up, ships and all.
texts.room-is-a-camera: A carafe of water on the washstand holds a whole harbour the right way up. On the bed and walls the same harbour hangs upside down, let in by one hole in the shutter.
texts.room-of-swallows: Eighty-six swallows are painted on the walls of a small upstairs room in a Bronze Age house on Thera. They peel off the plaster in pairs, leaving pale outlines behind, and touch beaks in the air. At the end all of them leave by the window in one ribbon.
texts.room-turning-red: No bigger than a bee, we cross a dining room that is being repainted a new colour around us. Whatever the wet paint goes round keeps a thin halo of the old colour, and the last strokes close on the window frame just as we reach it.
texts.running-wall: The animals on the cave wall are running. Horses and aurochs slide along the torch-lit rock trailing extra legs, then peel off its edge at the cave mouth and gallop on across a gorge drawn the way they are.
texts.saguaro-serigraph: Printed in flat inks like a 1930s national park poster, the Sonoran desert starts to move. Pronghorn gallop between saguaros whose shadows are bars of overprinted ink, and the floodwater a far storm sends down a dry wash arrives as one sliding shape.
texts.salmon-falls: Just ahead, a tail beats. It is one sockeye among thousands heading up the Brooks River in Alaska, and we are another. The river is three times life size, and so are the bears where it pours over a ledge.
texts.salt-wind-city: One sail of woven reed fills and swings round its post. It is one of a ring on a windmill built like a carousel, and hundreds of these turn over the salt pans. The pagoda beyond them has a ring of sails on each floor.
texts.same-field-every-hour: Dabs of oil paint with no outlines make up one Normandy valley, and a whole day is laid along it, dawn at the grainstacks and dusk a kilometre east.
texts.sapphire-moulin: Meltwater has sawn a canyon into the Greenland ice sheet. The blue river in it runs flat out through five bends to a shaft 325 metres deep and pours in.
texts.sauropod-ford: Legs are the columns and bellies the roof of a hall that walks, a herd of sauropods wading a braided river. We go through it on the back of a crested pterosaur.
texts.scale-tree-mire: Forty scale trees, 35-metre poles of diamond-patterned bark, stand in two rows in black water that doubles them. We go down the aisle as a griffinfly, a giant cousin of the dragonfly, while a river breaks its bank and floods in between the trunks.
texts.scholars-shelves: A magpie hops ahead through a painted Korean bookshelf and grows as the rooms do. Each is bigger than the one before, until books stand in stacks like pagodas.
texts.scratched-kalahari: Springbok stand along a game trail between Kalahari dunes and a porcupine turns its quills on whatever circles it. All of it is drawn on solid black, each quill and grass blade one white scratch.
texts.sea-sets-in-shade: Cloud shadow sets the swell hard and pale, and sunlight melts it clear and running again. A wax boat with a coral sail keeps to the lane of light.
texts.sea-stands-open: Above a tea stall's parasols a steamer's red bottom and turning bronze screw show in a wall of water. The sea is cut open in a straight dry lane from the beach to the lighthouse island, and the town uses it as a road.
texts.sea-turns-square: Bough by bough, a tree is being straightened as a lift carries us up through it. Above eye level the branches still curve, and below they are stairs of bars with panes of colour in the steps. Past it a city of flat planes floats over yellow avenues.
texts.seven-hundred-feet-of-ice: Far off, it is a pale line. Close to, it is a wall of ice 213 metres high, with a castle of timber halls huddled at its foot, a stair zigzagging up its face and fires burning along the top where men pace beside cranes.
texts.seven-rooms-one-clock: A masked ball winds through six of the seven rooms, each lit one colour by fires behind stained glass. When the clock in the last room strikes, everyone stops.
texts.seventy-eight-in-the-rain: We are small enough to ride a gramophone needle. The record under it is 300 metres across and runs past like a black road, while the tiled veranda of a house in Salvador stands still around us.
texts.shadow-theatre: At the back of a shadow theatre half a kilometre deep stands a palace of pierced card. Its four front walls split down the middle and slide apart, one after another.
texts.shaft-between-the-hexagons: Among the six-sided rooms, stacked without end round shafts of falling pages, there is one round room. Its wall is the spine of a single book, thirty metres high.
texts.shaken-globe: The glitter begins as sideways streaks, slows into a spiral and ends as plain snowfall on a village of blue-and-white porcelain. Reindeer rise and fall on its music-box carousel while, beyond the glass, something from the garden looks in at the size of a mountain.
texts.shoebox-reef: A string hauls a card turtle through a coral reef built in a cardboard box. Overhead a manta cut from a box lid beats its wings on brass fasteners, and two thousand kitchen-foil sardines turn on coat-hanger wire.
texts.shore-without-horizon: The tide comes in as a mirror. When it reaches the pale, smooth bodies balanced on their needle points they let go and rise like kites, each on a single hair, and their black shadows stay lying on the water.
texts.silent-engine: Brass rings, the widest a kilometre across, wheel above a pit on an airless world. At their centre hangs a star 40 metres wide, held by beams of light.
texts.silver-domes-and-streets-of-lead: Lead paves the streets in great dull plates, and the coloured lamps hung at the stalls lie in it as long streaks. Along the rooflines stand bronze figures, some winged and some crowned, each facing its own way.
texts.silver-dragon-bore: The Qiantang at Song-dynasty Hangzhou, where the autumn tide arrives as a wave four metres high from bank to bank. A sampan surfs it up to the city's water gate.
texts.singing-erg: White dunes under a black sky, and the only colour is light that crystal has split. Seven pillars of it, the tallest over 400 metres high, throw their fans into one bowl of sand, where they cross in a rose window.
texts.six-arms: We are small enough that the droplets of a cloud hang round us as glass globes. Among them one snowflake grows, burst by burst, until it is a star sixty metres from tip to tip. Then it falls out of the bottom of the cloud and we fall with it, toward the sea.
texts.sixty-fountains: We come up a lane on the one day a year a Japanese village of thatched farmhouses tests its fire cannons. Water goes up ahead of us the length of the valley. The largest house fires last, two jets crossing in an arch as pointed as its gable.
texts.sky-archipelago: A rope of cloud, three strands twisted together, climbs from a dark eye in the cloud sea into the underside of a floating island. On top, the island's lake pours over its rim in twelve waterfalls.
texts.sky-through-the-bone: Nothing casts a shadow and no sun shows. On a ridge stands one bleached vertebra, 250 metres tall, and three ravens fly ahead through the round hole in it.
texts.sledge-between-volcanoes: Two people in hooded coats and a sledge are going up a ramp of ice between a white volcano and a black one that is erupting. We overtake them below the icefall, and over the top their tent is already pitched and lit, with both their shadows on the cloth.
texts.sleeping-hill: An oak stands on top of a hill that is clear as glass right through, and its roots go down as far as its crown goes up, past three badgers curled asleep.
texts.slipway-blossom: Riveted steel runs overhead for 240 metres, the hull of a liner on her slipway. Then the timber props fall in a wave and the whole ceiling slides away to the water.
texts.slow-rain-sea: Each raindrop is a wobbling lens with the horizon upside down inside it. The drops sink at walking pace to a mirror sea, where every landing throws up a crown.
texts.smoke-turns-the-aspens: Smoke from smouldering leaf piles drifts through a wood made the way a potter would make it. Trunks and deer are white crackle glaze on a floor of black clay, and each leaf is a copper disc that stays dull green until the smoke reaches it.
texts.snow-ghosts: Rime has buried these firs so deep that each is a white figure with a drooped head, and all of them lean the same way, downwind. We ski down between them.
texts.snow-lattice-model: Underneath lies a floor of lacquered balls up to four metres across, on brass rods and steel springs. It is a chemist's model of ice the size of a city, still being built as loose water molecules tumble from the sky and click into the next row.
texts.snow-on-turquoise: A slab of snow lets go as we pass the great dome, slides down between its glazed blue-green ribs and bursts on the cornice. There are 64 of those ribs, each groove packed white, over a Silk Road city where pigeons from a rooftop loft fly ahead of us.
texts.snowbound-viaduct: Seven stone arches carry a steam train across a snowy valley at dusk, with a lantern hung under each keystone and a floodlit castle on the crag beyond.
texts.splashdown: Bolted to the outside of a capsule three metres tall, we come down from the black through fire, then silence, until three parachutes open above the sea.
texts.spore-rain: Seen from a beetle's back, a parasol mushroom is 36 metres tall. Spores sift from its gills and glitter where the wood's one beam of light crosses them.
texts.squall-of-light: Everything is laid in broad dabs of paint and turns about one low white sun. A fishing lugger passes close, then a small black paddle tug towing an old three-decker on a slack line. Ahead stands a squall: dark arms of cloud wound round the sun, the sea breaking, a brig and a fleet of luggers running for home, and beyond the brig a steam packet labouring, her smoke blown across the sun. Out of it a pale town appears: a lighthouse, a harbour mouth, arcades and domes, and a bridge of five arches whose middle arch is the way out.
texts.square-at-the-wrong-hour: Across the ochre ground lies the long shadow of a person, ending at a plinth with nobody on it. Bird shadows run up the white piers under an empty sky, and each shadow in town creeps to an hour of its own.
texts.stag-boulevard: Five decks of motorway cross one above another, wisteria trailing from every parapet and waterfalls dropping through the broken joints. We reach them at full gallop on a sika stag, mid-herd, down a flooded boulevard that mirrors glass towers furred with green.
texts.stair-that-points-at-the-pole: A palm squirrel a metre and a half long sleeps on a band of marble ruled with lead ticks, and wakes when the edge of a shadow passes over it. The shadow is cast by a wall shaped like a set square, its slope aimed at the pole so the yard can tell the time.
texts.stairway-everywhere: One waterfall drops, one runs sideways and one falls upward, and all three meet in a turning ball of water with giant goldfish inside. The stone stairs around it climb walls and cross ceilings under three suns.
texts.standing-sleepers: Sixteen metres of sperm whale hangs upright in open tropical water, fast asleep, the largest of a pod spaced in a ring like the stones of a henge. As we sink along her flank one eye opens.
texts.standing-tide: Clear water, pulled into a hill 300 metres high by a small moon passing just overhead. Fishing boats sail up its slope, and rays glide inside under the hulls.
texts.standing-wave-schlieren: Rock and pines are flat black cut-outs and the air itself is drawn, in hair-fine lines of two inks. Over an alpine ridge the lines pour down the far side and rear into a crest that holds still.
texts.star-with-one-blue-world: At first the planet is a dark bead on the face of a boiling white-gold star. At the end it slides onto that star, and the ring of fire round it closes to a full eclipse.
texts.still-lake-in-the-herd: A whaleboat with no harpoon in it is rowed through a circling herd of sperm whales to the still water at the middle, where cows and calves hang deep in the blue.
texts.still-on-the-sprue: Nobody has put this valley together yet. Its trees and animals hang as loose parts in frames of unpainted kit plastic, and snap themselves together as we pass.
texts.still-warm: In deep winter a Montreal row house is seen only as heat. Hot water runs gold inside its grey walls, and its people are fading prints of hands and feet.
texts.still-waving: In the back window things only get smaller. Telegraph poles and hedges slide in from the edges and shrink toward a white house, where someone at the gate keeps waving a cloth, and we turn to face the road only once the brow of the hill has covered them.
texts.stitched-country: One crimson thread makes this whole embroidered valley. The hills on either side come undone row by row so that a needle the height of a steeple can sew the road ahead.
texts.stone-face: The whole front of a building falls on us at the end of a street in a gale, and its one open window comes down exactly where we are. A piano has already missed.
texts.stone-knives: Limestone in Madagascar, worn into thousands of blades eighty metres tall. White sifaka lemurs cross it in leaps from one tip to the next, and so do we.
texts.stork-kettle-riso: Migration day over a headland, storks circling up a thermal while ships cross below. All of it is printed in three inks, and the white of the birds is bare paper.
texts.storm-bands: Living balloons up to 150 metres tall drift across the cloud tops of a gas giant, each with a blue-green glow inside. Where the cloud ends, more of them ride a cyclone's wall down in a spiral and sink into its well.
texts.storm-savanna: The sun is low and directly behind us, which puts a double rainbow dead ahead over the biggest baobab on the plain, and lights the grass and a file of elephants gold against a wall of thunderstorm.
texts.storm-that-drowned-no-one: Past the gale the island is calm, with a grove of lime trees and standing corn under a whole rainbow. Over the corn the clouds are shaped as great buildings, and each one sinks from its roof downwards and heaps itself up again in its own time.
texts.strait-between-two-rocks: On one side of the strait a dark mountain goes up into cloud. On the other, below a single fig tree, the sea drains into a funnel and wells back up.
texts.striped-tents-white-fire: Out in a dark meadow an iron fence makes a circle 380 metres across, its gate open. Tents stand inside it ring within ring, and the tallest holds cloud rising in steps to its open crown.
texts.stripes-in-the-grass: A tiger's stripes and the shadows between the grass stems are cut from one stencil, so she shows only while she moves and is gone again once she stops.
texts.study-at-mouse-height: At eighty times life size, a sea chart hanging off the table is a hillside of paper. The climb runs from the firelit floor to an oil lamp and an empty green bottle.
texts.sun-in-the-antlers: Wherever the elk's shadow crosses the snow it is night, with stars in it, and cabin windows light up until it has passed. The animal stands 940 metres at the shoulder, taller than the mountains, and its body is a window onto the night sky.
texts.sun-print-meadow: We ride a tuft of thistledown through a hedgerow made as a cyanotype, pale plants on dark paper. Our shadow slides over the ground ahead as a small pale star, and the line it draws fades back into the dark behind it.
texts.sunken-colossus: Coral has grown over the toppled statue of a giant. It lies on its side in 26 metres of water, a reef where its chest was and a shoal of fish living in the hollow of one eye.
texts.sweet-green-interior: Oil paint in seven colours and no outlines. Hills and capybaras alike are as smooth as rolled dough, and a railway runs down the valley to a cactus 127 metres tall.
texts.swordbill-round: On the tip of a petal a drop of water swells and falls. The petal belongs to a flower some four metres long, one of hundreds swinging on a single leaning tree. The cloud forest is fifteen times life size, and we cross it as a hummingbird, bill first.
texts.tables-under-the-falling-sky: A round dining room of a thousand candlelit tables under a glass dome, on a dead plain where the last red suns are being pulled apart. One table carries a brass 42, a towel, a cup of tea and a small yellow fish in a bowl.
texts.tempest-light: Swells four storeys high run under a last yellow slit of day. On a black rock among them stands a granite tower with two beams turning, and each sweep shows up the rain and the gannets flying through it.
texts.temple-of-artemis: On flat wet ground among reeds and willows stands a marble building more than a hundred metres long. Three fires burn on a long altar in the court before it, their smoke drifts along its north side, and a procession walks its round on the paving.
texts.tempo-fen: A gust from behind pulls the ticking reeds into step, patch after patch. Their glints join into bright lines and race downwind to a metronome 140 metres tall.
texts.tenfold-every-two-seconds: It begins with a kingfisher hung almost still in the air. From there the clock runs ten times faster every two seconds, until mountains roll in toward the shore like swell.
texts.the-branching: Reindeer lichen a finger high stands like a forest on an Arctic boulder. The view pulls back ten thousandfold, until a river is forking across the plain as the lichen did.
texts.the-calving: Eighty-five metres of ice leans out from the glacier and falls into the sea. The wave runs back through the floes, lifting each in turn with its penguins, and reaches our kayak last. Past the crest a low berg has rolled over into a sapphire arch.
texts.the-city-that-left: People at a road fence watch a river town lift out of its valley at dusk, bedrock and all, lights still on, leaving them a hole and a dry riverbed.
texts.the-desert-opens: Rain is falling on a red gravel plain in Namaqualand, on the first of six days that go by in forty seconds. The gravel greens over and comes into flower, and each day the daisy heads swing round after a racing sun and shut at dusk.
texts.the-green-room: Seen from the nose of a surfboard, a fifteen-metre reef wave is a tunnel. Water climbs one wall, crosses the roof and falls on the other side as a curtain.
texts.the-ground-turns: A star-trail photograph turned inside out. The stars stay sharp fixed points and the lamps across the bay are what draw arcs, while the headland tips toward morning with its sleeping cottage.
texts.the-leader: Thirteen thousandths of a second, made to last forty seconds. Rain hangs over a rough sea as glass beads while one bolt of lightning steps down through it, fork by fork.
texts.the-light-comes-on: It is dark inside the fridge. We are a fruit fly in there with one green standby light, until the bulb comes on behind a whole city of glass jars and the door, 400 metres tall, starts to swing away.
texts.the-long-swan: A swan took so long over the finish line of a steamboat race that the judge's photo has it half a kilometre from tail to red bill, one foot recorded sixteen times.
texts.the-murmuration: A flooded fen, flat to a far tree line. Over it about a hundred thousand starlings fly as one body up to 600 metres long, and we are one of the birds.
texts.the-red-weed: Washing hangs on a line in an empty Surrey village. A red plant has choked the river and climbed the walls, and a machine on three legs is wading past.
texts.the-same-minute: First a tram comes down the hill and cuts across our line, losing the balloon tied to its brass pole. Eighteen seconds later we come down the same hill, cut across a tram that is climbing, and lose ours.
texts.the-sea-above: Whale shadows cross a wheat field. The whales are overhead, in an ocean hung 120 metres up where the sky ought to be, and the largest dives out of it.
texts.the-sounding: The dark is total, and the submersible sees by sonar. Each ping draws the trench walls in lines that fade within seconds, while anything alive shows as amber points.
texts.the-street-goes-up: Down, in this harbour town, is whichever ground is nearest. The land is bent once at a right angle, and past the bend the terraces point their roofs out to sea and barges ride a canal that runs straight up, while the steamers anchored offshore stay upright.
texts.the-striking-hour: Seen at the scale of a mouse, a tower clock spends a long while only ticking, its wheels stepping and standing still. Then the gear that rings the bell lets go, and we are thrown round a blur of spinning vanes and up the hammer wire into a bell 34 metres across.
texts.the-tall-cloud: Somebody's straw hat has blown off a hilltop washing line and rides the wind across a hand-painted plain of flowers, into the shadow of one cloud the height of the sky. There it changes to a second set of paints.
texts.the-throat: It begins as a small ball over the sea at dusk with the next world showing inside. The ball is a wormhole, and as it swells the two change places, until the far world is the whole sky and the sea we crossed is one thin thread round its edge.
texts.the-toppling: We ride a glass marble on a child's track of stair rods and cotton reels, beside a falling line of dominoes in a house built 25 times life size. Where the track ends the marble leaps and flies the length of the hall, and a fan of tiles below opens into a picture.
texts.the-turning-night: Nothing in this sky holds still. Thick oil strokes wind round each star in rings and roll through one great double spiral above a river village, until the whole of it drains into the halo of an orange crescent moon like water down a plughole.
texts.the-umbra: Fourteen kilometres up, a research jet flies among the storm tops on long straight wings. Then the Moon's shadow crosses the cloud and the sun goes black.
texts.the-unspilling: Steam sinks back into the kettle spouts, and a copper tray rolls up the aisle of an old Istanbul pastry kitchen built twelve times life size. It lifts off the marble, what it dropped mends in the air and lands on it, and the lot slides home onto its shelf.
texts.the-valley-unzips: Denim, seamed and riveted, makes the hills, and down the valley runs a zip a mile long. Behind its church-sized slider the cloth rolls back off the lining.
texts.the-way-back-round: Straight ahead leads back to the start. The tree that fills the sky like a mountain shrinks as we cross the water, until it is the island we left, with left and right changed over and the same birds coming down in its shallows.
texts.thermal-cold-wake: Seen as heat from orbit, the Gulf Stream is a magenta river against indigo, orange along its warm side. One of its loops narrows to a hairline at the neck and snaps, and the ring it leaves goes on turning by itself.
