texts.thousand-kite-roofs: Over a square kilometre of flat roofs in a Gujarati walled city, paper kites hang on lines that lean back to somebody's terrace. We are one of them, until a rival cuts our line and the wind takes us.
texts.thousand-lagoons: We fly as one black skimmer in a line of more than a hundred, lower bill held open in the water, cutting a furrow across one rain lagoon after another and lifting over the white dunes between.
texts.thousand-li-blue-green: Paint is still running down these mountains, a coat at a time, from the ridges into the hollows. Below them a bridge on a hundred trestles rules one line across a lake of bare silk.
texts.three-avenues-under-the-floor: Small boats are being rowed across a black lake to a palace where the shadows of dancers turn in the lit windows. The way there begins on a stair under a bed and runs beneath trees lit by their own leaves, with no sky above.
texts.through-the-tower: Washing hangs from the balconies of a housing block nineteen storeys tall. The monorail runs straight through it, by a hole five storeys high.
texts.tideline-cloister: The waterline runs across the middle of the view. Above it a canoe's prow slides through arches of mangrove root, and below it the same roots go on down to where young sharks cruise and five thousand silversides turn in one ball.
texts.tiled-cockerel-kitchen: The picture painted along the kitchen wall runs out of wall. Thousands of its tiles lift off, fly round the corner and settle on the next wall, where it goes on.
texts.tissue-and-balsa-meet: A sheet of yellow tissue is being laid over the bare ribs of a hilltop with nobody laying it, and it pulls tight as it goes. Hundreds of rubber-powered models turn in a column above, the highest 300 metres up.
texts.titan-strait: An ichthyosaur 25 metres long swims a metre or two under the surface, in water so clear and shallow that her shadow travels beside her on the pale sand. She rolls toward us and blows a low puff of breath, white against the red shore.
texts.towers-over-the-old-city: Midwinter sunrise over an empty river city under snow. We come in low across drifting ice, over a bridge crowded with houses, up the west front of the great church, between its two towers and down to its south door, while bars of cloud take the sunlight off the stone and let it fall again.
texts.town-from-all-sides: A goods train crosses nine arches in front of a town whose walls and roofs keep coming apart, since each flat plane shifts with where we are. Before the middle arch there is a line where they all meet, and for two seconds the town is solid.
texts.town-kept-up-by-fans: The houses are sewn from ripstop nylon and each is kept up by a fan. The trees along the avenue are 25-metre tubes with waving arms, and when the castle loses pressure and sags, carts trailing hoses race in to pump it back up.
texts.treetop-giants: The old cow drags a poplar bough down with her lip and lets it whip back in a burst of yellow leaves. She is a rhinoceros with no horn, 4.8 metres at the shoulder, and she chews with one small eye on us.
texts.tulou-rings: Five tiled roofs, each a hollow loop, stand out of the mist like craters in the tea hills of Fujian. A swallow's lap inside one of them passes tiers of wooden galleries, then drops low over the market in the court, where the hens scatter.
texts.turned-country: Lacquered wood off a lathe makes up the whole country, so each hill and cloud is round about its own axis and only what spins can stand. The tall peak in the middle unscrews, and there is another inside it.
texts.twelve-metre-tide: Six hours of a giant spring tide go by in less than a minute. We watch from a small blue fishing boat that starts aground on the floor of a Breton harbour and is lifted, past the weed and the ladders on the granite quay, to the level of the market square.
texts.twenty-floods: From the bow of a stone barge on a dead-straight canal, twenty years pass in forty seconds. The fields flood and ripen and a pyramid goes up, then is cased in white.
texts.under-the-snow-roof: Overhead a fox is digging, and its head and then one paw come down through the ceiling. The ceiling is the snow on a Lapland fen, the tunnels beneath are seen from three centimetres tall, and near the end a great grey owl comes through feet first.
texts.unrolling-wood: Along a stream of blue paper strips the fiddleheads wind shut as we pass. Only the largest coil springs open, and it straightens into a frond with us on it.
texts.unstrung-falls: We ride a moth of beaded wire. It climbs a gorge stitched from glass beads to a waterfall of loose pearls, and above the fall hangs their source, a necklace on a frayed thread that keeps dropping balls eight metres wide.
texts.uphill-to-black: When the engines cut out, the spent booster slides away behind us and turns over against the planet with its fins unfolding, in a glitter of ice. It has carried us from a launch pad by the sea up through the cloud to where the sky is black and the horizon curves.
texts.upward-falls: Storm light and a gale on a turquoise lake in Patagonia. Each gust catches the waterfalls on the granite wall from below and carries them up over the rim as banners of spray. Then the water comes back down.
texts.valley-of-falls: A waterfall drops 500 metres in three tiers down a granite wall at the head of a glacier-cut valley. Partway up the river a scrap of rainbow shows in the waterfall's spray, and by the plunge pool it has grown into an arch.
texts.walking-dune: The dune moves by sending its sand over the crest one cube at a time. At the foot of the far face twelve palms, buried to the crown, are being dug out, and beyond them a dome and a chequered floor are coming clear.
texts.water-clock-city: The manuscript page is as big as a city. Water machines are drawn on it in black ink and flat colour, cut open to show their tanks, and they work, so that when a bowl sinks inside the elephant a falcon lets a gold ball fall into a serpent's jaws.
texts.waterspout-sisters: The thinnest of the waterspouts stretches into a rope and is drawn back up into the cloud, and a new one touches down further along, so there are still five. We slalom between them in a biplane, then climb in a spiral round the greatest.
texts.weight-of-glass: Weight is what colours this glass. A 260-metre arch of it stands in a shallow sea with a peacock eye of bands at each foot, where the whole load comes down.
texts.well-of-rain: Water is going down a shaft in the forest one leaf at a time. Each leaf is a basin twenty metres across that fills until it tips into the next, then springs back. The drop is 860 metres and ends in a rainbow closed into a full ring.
texts.wells-over-the-buried-lake: The green stops exactly where the water under the rock stops, in one curve across a dry plain. Inside the curve a well in each yard goes down to the dark lake.
texts.whale-fall-garden: Where a rib meets the spine, an octopus sits with its arms curled back over itself. The rib belongs to a blue whale, 27 metres of skeleton lying on its back two hundred metres down, with red worms growing on the bone in tufts and coral trees standing round it.
texts.what-happened-here: New snow on a wide field, and not an animal in sight. We cross it along one bird's prints, at whatever speed the bird was going when it made them.
texts.what-the-frog-sees: Frogs see only what moves. When we stop on the mud the pond goes blank, a pale field with thistledown falling through it, and a tall bird comes closer, seen only while it is taking a step.
texts.what-the-ocean-builds: Flakes of pale froth fall past. They come off the arches of a hall six hundred metres long, which the black sea below has just thrown up out of itself. The far end is still growing as we fly in, and before we are out the roof has begun to sag.
texts.wheel-of-life: Each salmon is a statue on a brass peg, cast one instant further into its jump than the one behind. When the whole terraced wheel spins fast enough, the fish leap.
texts.where-circles-hum: Triangles stand as a mountain range and nine ruled strings as a harp, with no ground under them. Flat circles make a third colour where they overlap, and inside the largest, a black one, the field goes dark.
texts.where-horses-are-blue: We run at fox height, and the first horse is over ten metres at the shoulder. It lifts its head and steps back to let us pass beneath. Further on a yellow cow with blue patches jumps clean over the path, and a whole herd gallops down the valley around us.
texts.where-the-page-was-folded: Folded on wet ink and now pulled open, the sheet rises on both sides like valley walls. Each splash on one wall has its twin on the other, so from the crease the whole view is one symmetrical figure.
texts.where-the-pattern-falls: Somewhere in a 250-metre drop the black and white rectangles lose their corners and take on colour, and what lands is a disc or an eight-petalled flower.
texts.whiplash-wind: Hair is being wound onto a disc 120 metres across on the highest hill and held there with two crossed gold hairpins. The woman has gone from the art-nouveau poster, and her hair blows over the hills in her place.
texts.wind-draws-the-namib: A gust like the flat of a hand wipes a whole dune off a sheet of lit glass, and the sand it threw up settles into a herd of gemsbok, hooves first and horns last, already at full gallop. They run on across the bare glass, each stamping a row of prints behind it.
texts.wine-dark-cup: We cross the inside of a Greek drinking cup nearly a kilometre across, with galleys rowing on its painted sea. As we round the largest ship a line creeps along its hull, the light and dark of the painting change places, and the white sail stays white.
texts.wood-behind-the-coats: Between the fur coats in a wardrobe there is a gap, and through it snow is falling on a forest where one iron street lamp burns in a drift. Further in, a frozen stream thaws as we follow it, and flowers open in a wave ahead of us.
texts.world-turtle: A small sun rides a golden hoop around a country of forests and one city, and day turns to night there inside a minute. The country is the shell of a swimming turtle.
texts.written-range: Across a seismograph's chart nearly two kilometres wide, 140 pens are still writing, and each ridge of these mountains is one pen's line standing up as a curtain of paper.
texts.zeus-at-olympia: At dawn the sun comes in by the one door and lies along the floor as far as a black pool of oil and the golden knees of a seated god. The rest of him goes up into the dark, lit by six small lamps.
texts.the-blank-answer: A night city where every wall is a board of coloured squares on black: a puzzle, or its answer. As you fly the street the answers fill in beside their questions, a small game plays itself on the floor, an arch opens and a stepped pyramid lights its windows. On the summit the last board is left open, and that is the way out.
texts.no-colour-on-colour: A country painted like a coat of arms, in five flat colours and two shining metals, where colour never lies on colour. A gold lion the size of a hill walks the green castle wall, roars over the river and the tournament camp, and rears beside the ring you leave by. Whatever crosses a dividing line swaps its colours.
texts.liquid-crystal-squall: A sea at sunset printed in three flat inks, like the glass of an old liquid-crystal pocket screen where every shape is a segment that is on or off. A black five-masted ship leans from one pose to the next, a striped lighthouse turns its beams, and you round her stern toward a half sun with gulls flying across it.
texts.half-coloured-regatta: A seaside regatta inside a colouring book, printed in black line and coloured in with felt-tips as you fly. The fleet sails its course and leaves. One burning motor launch never races: it circles the same three marks for ever, and every lap sends another rosette to a tower of prizes under a gold cup.
texts.three-pegs-in-the-valley: You come in low past a great stone ring still half cut from its quarry wall. Three rock needles in a red desert pass five stone rings between them, one at a time, by the old puzzle's rule, and each ring's holed shadow slides over the sand. Up the valley stand three giant needles whose rings hang caught, lie broken or have fallen. You round one fallen ring and fly toward the sun, through the hole of a huge ring that hangs turning in the air.
texts.muffins-that-look-back: Four baking tins the size of a county sit on a checked tablecloth, sixteen golden domes in paper cases. Nine are blueberry muffins. Seven are chihuahuas, and now and then one lifts its head to look at you. You pass a three-tier cake with gingerbread men circling it and leave by the round door of a gingerbread house.
texts.every-last-wire: A green farming valley is being unmade into paperclips. From the middle outward the trees, hedges and houses come undone into wire that runs to a ring of reels, and clips stand in rows where the crops were. A chain of great clips climbs in one arc to a clip as tall as a tower, and you leave through its top loop.
texts.loom-of-numbers: An engine that was never built stands whole at the size of a cathedral, at work with nobody in it. You come in high under a glass vault over ranks of golden number columns, pass a great flywheel, circle a round hall where bright ripples climb the columns, and leave through a loom weaving flowers and leaves.
texts.flavian-amphitheatre: Rome in the year 80, a morning of the opening games of the amphitheatre later called the Colosseum. You cross the open ground with the crowds, climb beside its wall and come over the rim into the full bowl. The arena is flooded, as one writer told it long after: horses and bulls swim in a ring and six oared boats hold station.
texts.pelican-peloton: A road race of pelicans on bicycles along a picture-book coast, in flat colour and one thick ink line. You overtake the whole field from the back, where the bicycles are drawn all wrong, past a harbour of diving pelicans, to the one right pelican at the front. The road lifts off into the clouds and runs straight into the sun.
texts.over-the-wall-on-a-box: An autumn valley built as a tin toy on a workbench, its painted hills rising and falling on posts. Clockwork hares have shut themselves in a walled orchard, and clockwork foxes ride apple crates over the wall to find them. One fox goes over beside you. You pass a brass sun and two great wheels and leave through a giant crate.
texts.basalt-organ-cave: A sea cave built of tall six-sided stone columns, packed like organ pipes, its water lit green from below. A swell carries you in from the open sea just above the surface. The cave drains under you, past seals on the broken steps, and floods back. Then the next wave throws you up the blowhole and out into the sky.
texts.sown-with-cloth: A bare mountain valley drawn in pencil and charcoal on pale card, where the only colour is cloth and all of it moves in the wind. You skim a field planted with thousands of small turquoise flags as cranes get up beside you, then sweep up inside a cone of violet ribbons strung from a rock tower. A green banner nine hundred metres long streams off a snowy peak, and you climb along it to the ring it flies from.
texts.stair-that-doubles: A stair at night, cut from blue stone and white paper, where every step is twice the size of the one below and holds a paper thing twice as great: a folded boat, a rocking horse, a chair, a clock, a hut, a windmill, a ship, a viaduct, a cathedral. Gold numbers on the walls double with them. You climb past them all, fly under the viaduct among paper birds, and go in at the cathedral door to a nave hung with lanterns.
texts.peak-above-the-singing-fields: A sunny spring meadow of new grass and tiny flowers under a single mountain whose head is lost in white cloud. You fly over a shelf of great grey wind-shaped stones and a garden on a clear river, then round and up the rock face as the sky darkens with every metre of height. You pass through the cloud and come out at the bare top, where a huge white moon hangs over a far sea of cloud and the sky is thick with stars.
texts.where-the-lattice-grows: The inside of a growing crystal, drawn in points and threads of light. Rows of gold lamps run away to one white spark, and on the cold side great snow crystals turn slowly in a blue and violet deep. You pass the largest of them close, then fly down the middle of a rose of six-sided rings, ice blue through gold to ember red, to the spark at its heart.
texts.wooden-sea-stage: An old court theatre in the middle of a change of scene, seen from inside its own wooden machinery. Under the stage, men walk a great capstan round to turn seven carved rollers into waves. You rise through the open floor beside a painted sea serpent, meet a gilt sun coming down in its clouds, watch a ship sail between the painted wings, then fly out over the footlights into a candlelit horseshoe of red and gold boxes and see the whole storm from the front as it turns to dawn.
texts.airship-shed-dawn: First light in a vast iron shed where a great silver airship lies. You start under its tail fins, fly the length of its back beneath the roof trusses toward the opening doors, and come down its flank past an engine car as ground crews in long files walk it out. Outside, the meadow is gold with low sun and long shadows, and you go ahead to the ring on the mooring mast as a second ship passes overhead.
texts.night-shining: A research balloon at the edge of space over the polar pack ice at midnight. You begin looking straight down past its gondola as a silver thread of ballast pours away toward the cracked ice, then lift off and turn up along the ladder and parachute to the great clear balloon standing on the curve of the world, with aurora or night-shining clouds behind it and a sister balloon far off. You climb its flank as meteors cross the stars, and at the top the balloon tears open like a flower and you rise through its petals.
texts.iron-tower-first-night: Paris at dusk in 1889, the year of the world's fair, with the Eiffel Tower new and painted red. You come down the river and under a stone bridge, fly in between the tower's four legs as its gas lamps come on, and climb round it. From the top you look out over the lit city to the palace across the river, then draw back until the whole tower stands over the fair with fireworks beside it, and run down the garden past coloured fountains to the gateway in its great arch while the iron glows red with Bengal fire.
texts.stone-on-the-fifth-line: A game board the size of a country lies under a film of still water at dusk. Nineteen dark causeways each way rule a rose mirror, and thirty-six smooth stones as big as hills, slate and shell, stand on their own reflections, with two wooden bowls of spare stones in the mist beyond. You dive in from high above, see the whole board, and fly low between the stones. Every half minute one more stone comes down out of the sky onto its point: a crown of water stands round it, rings run out and break white on the causeways, and thousands of rose wading birds go up.
texts.the-yard-goes-green: A railway signal yard at night in rain, drawn as light on black. Every lamp is red when you arrive; they turn green ahead of you as you fly, file by file and up a tower of lamps tier by tier, until one last red lamp at the end of a cutting falters, turns, and is the way out.
texts.the-fire-comes-round: A wall of flame crosses the whole horizon, and it never goes out: it travels round this world for ever. You fly up a dark river between giant plants hung with amber lights while long-legged herds wade away from the fire, run along the burning front with black trunks doubled in the water, then turn to a castle that pours water over its own walls.
texts.hollow-of-the-wave: A Japanese woodblock print of the open sea, and you fly into it: three blues on cream paper, every crest ending in claws of foam. You skim the swells past long yellow rowing boats, drop into the trough beside a wall of water 46 metres tall, and fly the whole length of its hollow while the lip throws over you and a small red mountain is printed in the opening ahead.
texts.fields-of-gazing-grain: A slow ride on the box of an open carriage behind two grey horses, with nobody driving, along one country road where the hours of a day are places. You pass a white school and its emptied yard in afternoon sun, ripe wheat with every ear turned to the road, a red sun going under over still water, a blue meadow of dew and mist, and an old oak under the moon. The road runs on between two floods full of stars toward a line of first light that never comes nearer.
texts.city-doubled-in-its-lake: A city of verandas climbs the shore of a still lake, and under the water hangs the same city upside down, as solid as the one above. Stairs with lanterns walk straight down through the surface, and every arch of the long bridge meets its twin to make a whole ring. You fly along the quay, tip over a balustrade to look down a well of houses that go on below the waterline, and leave from the end of a jetty.
texts.envelope-at-dawn: You fly low over a dawn meadow where balloons stand ready, and in through the mouth of one that still lies half filled on the grass. Inside, the burner roars, the cave of coloured cloth rounds out, and the whole vault swings upright around you and lifts off. You look straight down past the basket to the river, slip out under the rim into a sky full of other balloons, and come back in from above through the open valve at the crown.
texts.cloud-in-the-cave: Son Doong in Vietnam is the largest cave passage known, and where its roof fell in long ago the sun gets in and a jungle grows inside the mountain. You fly up the cave's river by the light of cavers' lamps, past golden stalagmites as tall as towers and steps of turquoise pools, and out through the mouth into sunbeams and drifting cloud. Then you cross the pool under a waterfall and climb a staircase of small pools between flowering trees to the way out.
texts.the-digging-wheel: A digging machine the size of a cathedral stands in an open pit and eats its way into a hill of ripe barley. You cross the pit floor past a parked coach that looks like a toy beside it, fly along the boom to the great toothed wheel as it bites the edge of the field, and come up over the lip beside a farmhouse the wheel has almost reached. In the next field a combine and a tractor are bringing the harvest in.
texts.blue-fire-crater: Kawah Ijen in East Java is a volcano's crater where sulphur gas burns blue in the dark. At three in the morning you come in over the rim beside a fall of burning sulphur and follow a river of blue fire down the slope to a milky turquoise acid lake. Then you fly low over the water between tall chimneys of yellow sulphur with flames at their tops, past an arch, to a fall of blue fire that comes down the whole height of the far wall.
texts.hands-in-the-painted-cave: A cave by lamplight, its walls covered in stencilled hands, the oldest kind of painting there is, all doubled in still dark water. Near the way in every hand has five fingers. Then one great black hand has six, and from there the count slips room by room, seven, nine, a dozen, until the far wall is a single hand with fingers all the way round like a sun. An in-joke on the pictures AI made in 2022 and 2023, when the quickest way to spot one was to count the fingers.
texts.pole-that-must-not-fall: Sunrise on a salt plain, printed in flat inks. A black and brass cart the size of a railway station runs to and fro on its track to keep a striped mast 480 metres tall from toppling, and each time it catches it. Around it a school of small carts practise with poles of their own, and every so often one comes down. An in-joke on the cart and pole, the balancing task that has been a first lesson for learning machines for decades.
texts.car-that-must-back-up: A long valley cut from blue paper stands on a table of light in the hour after sunset. Along the cut edge of every sheet a heavy rack car, too weak to climb the far ridge, backs away from it up the wrong slope, again and higher, until it comes down through the bottom and over. More than a hundred do it at once, each a few seconds behind its neighbour, so the whole valley swings as one slow wave.
texts.half-city-of-the-fair: A city of two halves on an open plain in the last minutes of sun. One half is a great fair, its big wheel of hanging cages, its switchback railway and its chain swing all turning with every lamp lit, rooted like an old town. The other half is a proud town of marble and stone that stands on skids, with lifting rings in every cornice and its outermost fronts already roped onto long trailers.
texts.roofs-of-the-old-stone: Sunset over a castle so vast that its roofs are a country: acres of slate, a field of flagstones in the sky, towers like knuckles and one like a broken finger. A dead tree grows straight out of a wall with a tea table set on it, a white tide of cats runs along a parapet, and rooks rise in storms.
texts.to-the-brim: A candlelit banqueting hall four times life size, laid for a feast nobody has come to: more than five thousand wine glasses on long tables, a tiered pyramid and shelved walls, every one poured exactly half full. You fly down the tables and round the pyramid to one great glass on a dais, where a decanter is pouring. The wine climbs past the line, swells above the rim into a trembling dome, and holds.
texts.ten-past-ten: A clockmakers' hall of iron and glass on a bright morning, built four times life size: more than a thousand clocks on walls, galleries, posts and chains, every pendulum swinging and every dial stopped at ten past ten. You round a great pendulum and fly down a shed where watches hang like slow rain. Only the two red hands of the glass dial at the far end move, and they meet at twelve as you fly through its hub. An in-joke on AI pictures of clocks, which nearly always show ten past ten.
texts.sky-with-a-seam: From the bow of a small boat we leave a too-tidy harbour over mirror-calm water. A cloud on ropes rains on one patch of sea. Then the horizon comes too soon: the sky is a painted wall, and we sail along it to where one seam stands parted on a lit backstage.
texts.otter-in-the-window-seat: A plain white airliner above sunset cloud, and everyone aboard is an otter. We arrive as the signal: over the roof, past sea otters afloat on a cloud top and one sliding down the wing, in at a window and up the aisle, where laptops wake row by row. The way out is the last otter's screen.
texts.pallet-tower-midsummer: A round tower of wooden pallets 47 metres tall stands on a rock off a Norwegian shore, ringed by hundreds of waiting boats. We circle it once while fire comes down from its top and the evening sun gives way to blue dusk, until the whole burning pillar leans and falls into the sea.
texts.floor-without-windows: We leave a white lobby behind glass, cross a round well ringed with floor upon floor of lamp-lit desks, and come out over a whole city of office towers standing between one floor and one endless ceiling of lights. No window looks outside, there is no sky, and nobody sits at any desk.
texts.bronze-walled-island: From the bow of a dark ship we pass under a great arch of pale rock and out among tall sea stacks on a violet evening sea, the low sun behind them. Then a whole island comes up ahead: sheer cliffs with a wall of bronze all the way round the top, and roofs, trees and smoke inside it.
texts.harvest-in-profile: A giant head in profile, built entirely of vegetables and fruit, stands over a garden at dusk: a gourd for a nose, a pumpkin brow, a beard of bean pods. We come in low past wheat sheaves and cabbages, cross a lily pond with a great pumpkin on it, look up through sunflowers, then rise to the face and fly out through its open mouth.
texts.the-other-side-of-town: A small-town street on an autumn night, every porch and tree strung with coloured bulbs, and waves of light running through them under a full moon. Then we pass through a tall leaf of white light standing in the road, into the same town frozen and colourless under the northern lights, where a pale ghost of every bulb still blinks. We rise over the white roofs and come down the frozen main street to the way out.
texts.garden-behind-the-ivy-wall: From a winter moor we come up a walk between old brick walls to a green door standing open under a curtain of ivy. Behind it lies a walled garden in every season at once: grey bare stems by the door, then crocuses and daffodils, cherry blossom, and roses in full bloom at the far end.
texts.railway-under-the-sea: A single track lies just under clear, ankle-deep water that reaches every horizon. A small yellow rail-bus draws past and we follow in its wake, past herons, a timber beacon and a low marsh island with thatched houses. It stops at a halt on piles; then a high veil turns the sun silver inside a halo, and the rails run on alone under the mirror to the ring.
texts.boathouse-full-of-morning: A tall blue police box stands on a lake at dusk, its lamp pulsing. We fly in through its open doors and come out in a walled garden in morning sun, far larger than the box. The same box stands at the end of the garden's canal, and through its doors lies a sunset sea with red sails and a harbour town. On an islet it stands a third time; its doors open on pack ice under a giant ringed planet, where the same blue box waits on a floe with the ring in its doorway.
texts.harbour-in-the-aurora: We fly low over broken sea ice in a polar night. Where the aurora hangs thinnest, a harbour city stands in full daylight behind it. The line climbs a ridge of piled ice into the moving curtain and comes out over warm blue water, then rises among striped towers, domes and palms with gulls wheeling round them. At the end the wall of night and its green lights stand behind the town.
texts.bells-before-breakfast: A great house of pale stone stands in its park at sunrise, with turrets at its corners, a tall tower in the middle flying a red flag, a cedar on the lawn and deer by the lake. We go in at the front door, through a hall with an open oak roof and a row of state rooms whose doors stand open in one line, a green drawing room and a library two storeys high. Then down into a vaulted kitchen full of copper pans, fires and steam, along a white passage, and into a hall whose whole end wall is a board of about a hundred brass bells, swinging round the way out.
texts.doors-in-transit: A great station shed of brick, iron and glass stands in morning sun. Doors of every colour and shape hang from overhead rails and travel through it in short trains, level above level, round a tower stacked with more. We fly up among them and come back down to a small tiled booth on the floor, where one white door painted with flowers has been set apart. It stands half open as we arrive, and the next place lies behind it.
texts.funnel-over-the-wheat: A straight gravel road runs through green wheat toward a huge turning storm. A tornado comes down off to the left, swells to a wide wedge with a ring of dust at its foot, crosses the road ahead and swings away north, thinning to a white rope. Then the road turns west: wet gravel shining toward a low sun, under a sky of glowing cloud pouches.
texts.after-rain-the-whales: It has just rained, and the low sun is on the glass towers of an everyday city. We fly up a tree-lined avenue at the height of the plane trees, and whales swim past in the air: a humpback and her calf at eye level, a pod strung along the street, dolphins among the tree tops, a blue whale crossing far ahead. Over a square six sperm whales sleep upright, orcas come the other way, and white whales circle the lamps of a flight of steps. The way out is a white stone arch on a terrace above a valley town.
texts.hall-roofed-with-weather: A great stone hall at night, lit by thousands of candles that hang in the air. Where the roof should be there is weather: a storm cloud inside the walls, with soft lightning glowing in it and rain that never reaches the floor. The flight passes a fire pit and long tables laid for a feast, runs along the tall arched windows, then climbs through the candles into the cloud, where the way out waits.
texts.comet-over-the-lake-town: A round lake in wooded mountains at dusk, so still that it mirrors the whole sky. Overhead a comet with a long fanned tail is breaking apart. The flight crosses the water to a small town of dark timber houses with lit paper windows, climbs its stone street, passes stone lanterns and fireflies in a meadow, and comes out over flooded rice terraces as the comet's pieces fall as a shower of meteors.
texts.houses-on-strings: A flat-topped mountain with a great waterfall, standing in a sea of cloud. Off its edge drifts a whole stone village: cottages, long barns and a windmill, each on its own timber raft, each hanging from a great cluster of coloured balloons. The flight rounds the cliff, passes close under the rafts and between the clusters, then follows the village out over the mountain's top of rock, pools and shrubs, where one small painted house hangs under a single great ball of balloons of every colour.
texts.mountain-of-four-elements: At sunrise one volcano stands in an icy polar sea. The flight climbs it from the water to the summit, and all the way up the mountain's own matter moves as if by an unseen hand: sea water lifted in frozen arcs, slabs of striped rock raised and set down again, arcs of fire over cracked lava, wind turning cloud and blossom into rings. At the top, white towers with blue tiered roofs stand on stone pillars above a sea of cloud.
texts.pyramid-of-khufu: At the height of the flood the Nile reaches a harbour at the desert's edge, with papyrus, palms and boats at the quay. A long causeway climbs from it to the plateau, where the pyramid stands new: about 146 metres of white casing stone under a capstone sheathed in gold, with three small queens' pyramids beside it and files of porters crossing the rock at its foot. The flight passes close along its faces and ends looking back over the flood toward a low sun.
texts.green-gate-past-the-poppies: A road of yellow brick runs between white fences and ripe wheat on a bright morning. It passes round-roofed farmhouses and old trees, dips through a sunken lane, and comes out into a great field of red poppies. Beyond the flowers stands a city built all in green, with a domed hall, a stepped tower and a long wall, and the road ends at its gate.
texts.city-closing-overhead: A town of brick terraces at dusk, its windows lit and its street lamps on. Ahead the ground does not end: the town bends upward, climbs like a wave and comes back overhead, so that streets, roofs and a tall tower hang upside down above the street you fly along. The flight rises between the two towns, looks out over the rooftops and the dark fields beyond, and comes back down to the street where the way out waits.
texts.town-round-one-stair: A whole town lives down one great concrete shaft. The flight starts in a service tunnel of rails, pipes and steaming plant, crosses a machine hall with flywheels, a water wheel and falling water, and climbs past rings of small coloured homes with lit windows, then farm terraces under violet grow lamps. At the top it goes out through the lid onto a dusty plain at sunset, where only low round roofs show above the ground and a ruined city stands on the horizon.
texts.asgard-bridge-of-light: A still sea ends in mid-air and falls away into the stars. At its edge a golden globe on a round terrace sends a beam of rainbow light up into the night. From it a straight bridge of rainbow light runs across the water to an island city built all in gold, crowned by a palace like a rank of organ pipes. The flight follows the bridge over the falling edge and the mirror sea, and climbs between the city's towers under a great moon.
texts.sea-of-loose-coin: A long hall of riveted steel under two strips of daylight holds a fortune as a sea of loose gold coin, in dunes and troughs from wall to wall. The flight starts low among the coins beside a depth gauge, passes under a tall white diving tower and its springboard, and climbs over a red footbridge to see the whole sea, with coin pouring from chutes along both walls. It comes down past a great sink where the coin spirals away and leaves by the round vault door, standing open.
texts.three-shadows-each: A frosted plain of stone spires and blue meltwater pools under three suns, so that every spire throws three shadows. A great stepped pyramid stands in the distance. As the flight winds between the spires toward it, the three suns draw together into a single row in the sky, and the ground lets go: loose stones and then whole blocks lift off the plain and drift upward.
texts.shoal-over-the-high-street: A cheerful small town on a sunny morning: painted shopfronts, striped awnings and bunting from roof to roof. Giraffes canter down the middle of the high street and giant red and white shrimp swim through the air above the chimneys. We follow the street into a square with a fountain and cafe umbrellas, where the giraffes circle, then rise past the clock tower, where ladybirds the size of dinner plates sit on the stone, and out over the roofs to the fields beyond.
texts.dial-towers-at-dusk: A city of tall stone bell towers at dusk, violet overhead and orange along the horizon, with lamps lit in the streets far below. Every tower carries a great clock dial and a bell in its open belfry, and every stroke of a bell goes out as a pale ring that widens over the roofs until the whole sky is laced with them. We fly between the towers, close past the bells and the dials, across a dark river, and leave between the last great clock faces.
texts.bridges-of-marigold: A city at night, built of bright little houses stacked on houses into towers that rise out of a dark misty gulf, every window lit. Bridges made of nothing but glowing orange marigold petals arc across the gulf and between the towers, shedding petals into the air. We cross the first bridge to the gate house, climb among the towers under lines of paper flags and coloured lamps while a cable tram passes, and leave from a rooftop market along one last bridge of petals.
texts.valley-inside-the-works: Under the iron and glass roof of a great brick factory lies a green river valley in flower, and its river and its waterfall are melted chocolate. Striped candy canes and spiral lollipops taller than trees grow from the grass among toadstools and fallen sweets, and a small pink boat rides the brown river. We follow the river past a great glass pipe that draws it up into the roof, climb beside the chocolate waterfall, and leave through a round window in the end wall wreathed in sweets.
texts.hill-of-round-doors: A soft green hill above a slow stream on a golden summer evening. Small homes are dug into its turf, each with one round door painted a strong colour, a brick chimney and a garden in flower. We cross a stone bridge beside a mill with a turning wheel, pass under a great tree hung with hundreds of paper lanterns where long tables are laid for a feast, and follow the lane up past the homes and their gardens to the last and highest of them, a round green door under an old oak.
texts.knee-deep-under-the-wave: A sea that is knee-deep all the way to the horizon, under a black hole ringed with bent light that serves as the only sun. Far ahead stands a pale mountain range, and it is a wave. A small landing craft lifts off the water as we pass and flies ahead; the wave comes on and swallows the black hole; we follow the craft up the streaming face, over the lit spray at the crest, and find the black hole whole again beyond it, growing as we fly on into it.
texts.lamps-under-the-roots: A wild island at dusk under a burning sky. The broken middle of an airliner lies on the beach beside a small camp; a dark stream leads up a gully into the forest, where a steel hatch lies in the ground with a shaft of light standing out of its glass. We cross the roof and fly down the lamplit court of a concrete station buried under great roots, past a tall radio mast with a red lamp, and come out into a green basin where an old sailing ship lies stranded far from the sea beneath a waterfall.
texts.shelves-of-lit-memories: The inside of a mind at night. Tall shelf walls curve away like the folds of a brain, every shelf a row of glass balls glowing gold, blue, red, green and violet. We dive beside a glass tube of racing balls into one lane, climb out over the wall tops to a round dark pit, cross its rim above a little train on a track of light, pass a funfair island on a tall stem with its great turning wheel under slow fireworks, and come to the tower in the middle of the pit and its one great glowing window.
